title: Microplate reader comparison: specifications and features
summary: Compare nine microplate readers across fluorescence, luminescence, TR-FRET, absorbance, plate handling, temperature control and ownership.
body_html:
Microplate readers can differ in their optics, detector behavior, timing and the options installed. Compare the configuration and measurement conditions alongside each headline specification. This matrix keeps the specifications, reader-specific notes and explanation of each finding together.

SpecificationsAt a glancePerformance charts

Fluorescence intensity

3 Fluorescence sensitivity, top, filters (fluorescein, converted to pM where the vendor gives a volume)

Filters are the sensitive path on every reader that has both. The number to compare is pM in a stated plate and volume; three vendors here print per-well amounts with no volume, or two different volumes on one sheet.

Fluorescence sensitivity, top, filters (fluorescein, converted to pM where the vendor gives a volume)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<0.15 pM / <3 amol (384 small-volume, 20 µL).

—
EnVision Nexus

<2 pM (module 1001, 485/535 nm; 50 µL, 384 OptiPlate) = 100 amol; a comparison sheet gives 200 amol. Flash count not stated.

Excitation exists at 340, 355, 400, 485, 535, 555 and 632 nm only. A dye in between has no module. The filter-module list is sparse.

PHERAstar FSX

<0.15 pM / <3 amol (384sv black, 20 µL). 1536: <0.5 pM (8 µL).

Free-air light path: lenses, no fiber bundles.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD5 only: 3 pM guaranteed, 0.5 pM optimized (384; volume not stated). iD3: no filters.

The iD3 has no filter path at all; every iD3 fluorescence read is a monochromator read.

Synergy H1

0.25 pM / 25 amol (384, works out to 100 µL). Manual guarantee: ≤10 pM (96-well; 3 pM typical in the IFU).

Filters read from the top only. The sheet figure is 40× better than the guarantee.

Synergy Neo2

0.2 pM / 4 amol (384 low-volume, 20 µL), typical. 1536: 1 pM (10 µL). BioTek’s brochure calls these “the average observed factory test values”; the 2016 manual (Appendix A) guarantees <5 pM filters and ≤20 pM monochromator, 25× and 10× the averages.

Sensitivity is qualified at Normal speed with 50 measurements per point; the 11 s sweep-mode speed on the same sheet comes from a different setting.

Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤25 amol in 100 µL = 0.25 pM. Enhanced: ≤8 amol in 10 µL (1536) = 0.8 pM. Calculated.

Quoted at fluorescein, the one color the standard module’s single 510 nm dichroic sits at. The manual’s binding spec for the standard module is <10 pM (40× the brochure).

VANTAstar

<0.5 pM / <10 amol (384sv, 20 µL).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not offered. Fluorescence intensity is monochromator only; the Varioskan’s filters serve luminescence, Alpha, BRET and TRF.

There is no filter path to fall back on when a fluorescence assay needs more light.

4 Fluorescence sensitivity, bottom, filters

Cell-based assays in clear-bottom plates are read from the bottom. Ask early whether the assay is read from the top or the bottom: on the Neo2 that exposes a build dependency, on the H1 it exposes the monochromator, on the Nexus three modes don’t read from below at all.

Fluorescence sensitivity, bottom, filters
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<1.0 pM / <50 amol (384 glass-bottom, 50 µL).

—
EnVision Nexus

Not published. Bottom FI is offered; the spec sheet gives no figure. “On-the-fly mode is not available when measuring from below.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

<1.0 pM (384g black, 50 µL). Same optic module reads top or bottom; autofocus.

From the bottom it still reads both emission colors at once, plus luminescence and Alpha.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not published for filters; the published bottom figure is the monochromator one (2.5 pM optimized).

Read height “should be optimized for each new lot of microplates or assay volume used.”

Synergy H1

Not offered. Filters read top only; every bottom read is a monochromator read.

—
Synergy Neo2

1 pM (100 µL, 384). Fixed bottom focus. Bottom reads need their own cubes and exist only on dual-top-PMT builds.

BioTek’s 2012 guide: bottom sensitivity “not demonstrated.” One bottom detector, so no simultaneous dual emission from below.

Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤500 amol (100 µL) = 5 pM. Enhanced: ≤180 amol (10 µL) = 18 pM. Calculated.

Twenty times the top figure on the same sheet.

VANTAstar

<2.5 pM / <125 amol (384g, 50 µL).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not offered (no filter FI).

—

5 Fluorescence sensitivity, top, monochromator

On every sheet here that prints both, the monochromator is less sensitive than the filters. The size of the loss differs: ~2× on the BMG readers, 2.6× on the Spark by Tecan’s own note, 10× on the Neo2 and H1 by Agilent’s own sheet.

Fluorescence sensitivity, top, monochromator
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<0.35 pM / <7 amol (384sv, 20 µL). Best monochromator figure published on any reader in this matrix.

The monochromator is about 2× less sensitive than the filters on the same sheet; the other readers lose 2× to 10×.

EnVision Nexus

Not offered. No monochromator in any mode.

—
PHERAstar FSX

No monochromator. Filter optic modules only.

Built for screening: every assay reads through a module made for its colors.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

6 pM guaranteed, 1 pM optimized (384; volume not stated). The iD3’s only fluorescence path.

MD’s own brochure rates its filters “10–40 times more sensitive than conventional monochromator based detection” in the near-IR. The iD3 has no filters.

Synergy H1

2.5 pM / 250 amol (384, 100 µL): 10× worse than its own filters. Manual guarantee ≤20 pM (96-well).

Fixed 16 nm band on most builds. A core facility taped a sign above its Synergy: “Please measure nano orange and mCherry plates with filter cubes, not with the monochromator!”

Synergy Neo2

2 pM / 40 amol (384 low-volume, 20 µL): ten times less sensitive than its own filters.

BioTek’s 2012 newsletter: “Filters are more optically efficient and will give you the best performance.”

Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤50 amol (100 µL) = 0.5 pM. Enhanced: ≤20 amol (10 µL) = 2 pM. Manual spec for the standard module: <20 pM.

Tecan’s own tech note prices its monochromator at 1.5–1.7× on one arm and 2.6× on both and calls that “comparable results.” The brochure figure uses the 510 nm dichroic; a dye away from fluorescein reads through a 50% mirror.

VANTAstar

<0.8 pM / <16 amol (384sv, 20 µL).

Under twice the filter figure (calculated).

Varioskan LUX

<400 amol per well (black 384; volume not stated) = 4 pM at 100 µL or 20 pM at 20 µL (calculated for both).

Its only fluorescence path, through an emission slit fixed at 12 nm. In a lab’s own PicoGreen QC test it failed the lab’s 20% CV limit; a fluorescein series across 3–400 amol read flat on it.

6 Fluorescence sensitivity, bottom, monochromator

Fluorescence sensitivity, bottom, monochromator
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<3.0 pM / <150 amol (384g, 50 µL).

—
EnVision Nexus

Not offered.

—
PHERAstar FSX

No monochromator.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

2.5 pM optimized (384), against 1 pM from the top: 2.5× weaker (calculated). Guaranteed bottom figure: not published.

—
Synergy H1

4 pM / 400 amol (384). Manual guarantee ≤20 pM (96-well). The only bottom path the H1 has.

—
Synergy Neo2

2.5 pM (100 µL, 384). Fixed bottom focus.

—
Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤800 amol (100 µL) = 8 pM. Enhanced: ≤220 amol (10 µL) = 22 pM. Calculated.

Enhanced monochromator: 20 amol top against 220 bottom on the same plate and volume, 11× worse from below.

VANTAstar

<3.5 pM / <175 amol (384g, 50 µL).

—
Varioskan LUX

<4 fmol (4,000 amol) per well: ten times less sensitive than its own top read. Nothing refocuses; the plate adapter sets the height.

At 100 µL that is 40 pM; at 20 µL, 200 pM (calculated).

7 Practical fluorescence dynamic range in one gain setting, without re-reading the plate

Take a plate whose brightest and dimmest wells are a million-fold apart. Readers that pick a gain per well inside the read see both at once; readers that fix a gain per read see one end and clip or lose the other, and the fix is a second pass. The Spark and Neo2 can widen effective range by reading the plate twice; that doubles the read time and breaks kinetic timing.

Practical fluorescence dynamic range in one gain setting, without re-reading the plate
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

8 decades in a single measurement (Enhanced Dynamic Range): a test flash picks a factory-calibrated gain per well, inside the delay the read already has.

Works in kinetics, with injectors and with a stacker. The user never sets a gain. Flying mode, the fastest read, runs at a fixed gain without EDR; in standard mode EDR’s test flash fits inside the pause the read already takes.

EnVision Nexus

No gain to set on the Ultra-sensitive photon counter and no published count-rate ceiling. Filter-path PMTs: no gain setting in any Kaleido 4.1 operation; the only bright-sample control it names is an “Attenuated” filter-module property.

None of the ten operation parameter lists in the Kaleido 4.1 manual (Rev E) has a gain, PMT-voltage or sensitivity entry, and the 2026 filter list (2321302) shows no module marked attenuated.

PHERAstar FSX

8 decades in one visit to the well (EDR). 700,000,000 counts.

Works in kinetics and with a stacker. Flying mode, the fastest read, runs at a fixed gain without EDR; in standard mode EDR’s test flash fits inside the pause the read already takes.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Kinetics run at a fixed gain chosen before the run, “a nominal dynamic range of three decades” per gain (MD, 2026). Endpoints get AutoPMT: a pre-read at High, then re-reads of saturated wells at Medium and Low.

MD’s own Figure 3: High saturates at 33 nM, Medium at 333 nM, Low is “losing sensitivity at low concentration.” The iD5 widens range for endpoints by re-reading saturated wells and, in fluorescence, by adjusting lamp intensity; it can’t do that in a kinetic or in luminescence. “For kinetic read, the PMT settings have to be fixed”; each gain covers “a nominal dynamic range of three decades.”

Synergy H1

A single read tops out at 99,999 RFU; the manual’s remedy for saturation is “Try lowering the gain/sensitivity” (read again). BioTek’s 2010 table gave 5 decades; the 2026 sheet says 7 for the same model.

Gain is set per read, by number or scaled to a well the user picks as brightest.

Synergy Neo2

Fixed gain per read, ceiling 10 million counts. “Auto-ranging” runs a gain check on every well and adds minutes per plate. BioTek support: use manual gain “for kinetic tests, rapid reads or for tests that require high sensitivity.”

Extended range by re-reading is possible for endpoints; for flash luminescence BioTek’s own tips say it is “simply not possible.”

Tecan Spark

One gain, chosen before the read, about 3–4 decades usable (inferred from Tecan’s help text). Tecan’s “extended dynamic range” is “Two consecutive measurement runs with a high and a low amplification” with the listed drawback “Long measurement times.”

Every one of Tecan’s four gain modes has a printed “Disadvantages” panel. Optimal mode: “If signal intensities within one plate are very far spread, certain signals might not be detected any more.” Two passes means the same well is read twice, at two moments; a kinetic can’t hold its timing. The two-pass method does widen the effective range for endpoints. Extended range is “Two consecutive measurement runs”; its listed drawback: “Long measurement times.”

VANTAstar

8 decades in a single measurement (EDR), gain set per well in <0.1 s.

—
Varioskan LUX

Auto gain picks one of four calibrated gains per well from a trial flash. Product page commits to FI >6 decades; the tech note shows seven.

Whether auto gain runs in kinetic reads: not published. The gain is chosen before the signal moves.

8 Who sets the detector gain, and when

When the user sets the gain before the read, a plate brighter or dimmer than expected has to be read again, and the time points of a kinetic run cannot be read again.

Who sets the detector gain, and when
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Nobody. EDR picks a calibrated gain per well from a test flash. Manual gain is available.

—
EnVision Nexus

No gain on Ultra-sensitive luminescence or HT Alpha (“Only one detector”). Filter path: no gain setting in any of the ten Kaleido 4.1 measurement operations.

Revvity does not say in words whether the filter-path PMT gain is fixed or automatic inside the instrument; Kaleido offers no control, and the “Attenuated” filter-module property is its only bright-sample lever.

PHERAstar FSX

Nobody on current units (EDR). Flying mode runs at a fixed gain.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

The user, before a kinetic (“the PMT settings have to be fixed”); AutoPMT for endpoints only. Two wavelengths lock the gain at High.

The “gain locked at High for multiple-wavelength reads” sentence comes from the SoftMax Pro 7.0.2 guide for the i3x; no iD guide confirms it yet.

Synergy H1

The user, per read: a number, or scaled to the well the user picks as brightest.

—
Synergy Neo2

The user, per read, or auto-ranging per well at a time cost.

—
Tecan Spark

The user, before the read, from four modes (manual, calculated from well, optimal, extended). Each mode has a printed disadvantage.

Optimal: “Signals between different runs might not be comparable.” Calculated from well: “If any signal intensities from another well are higher, the detector might be oversaturated.”

VANTAstar

Nobody (EDR).

—
Varioskan LUX

The reader, one of four gains from a trial flash before each well; kinetic behavior not published.

—

9 Detectors: how many, what kind, and whether two colors can be read at the same instant

Simultaneous dual emission means the two halves of a ratio come from the same flash, so lamp flicker and timing drop out of the ratio. Only two readers here do it as standard, and only one does it on identical detectors and from the bottom.

Detectors: how many, what kind, and whether two colors can be read at the same instant
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

One low-noise PMT; red-shifted PMT option to 900 nm; CCD spectrometer for absorbance. Two colors read one after the other.

—
EnVision Nexus

Two PMTs on the filter path (230–850 nm), simultaneous dual channel via dual-channel module. One PMT, 400–650 nm, on the Ultra-sensitive/HT-Alpha module, no filters. Photodiode for absorbance.

The most sensitive mode is one detector, one color, top only. BRET and any two-color luminescence drop to a less sensitive rung. The single-PMT “Nexus One” (2026) has no simultaneous pair at all.

PHERAstar FSX

Two matched pairs of PMTs (low-noise pair for FI/FP/lum; red-shifted pair for TR-FRET) plus a CCD spectrometer. Both channels of any ratio read at the same instant, top or bottom.

Simultaneous dual emission in FI, FP, luminescence, TR-FRET and Alpha, from the same flash, on identical detectors.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

One “ultra-cooled” PMT for every mode, emission to 850 nm. Two colors one after the other. Photocathode type not named.

A tube that reaches 850 nm is red-extended and carries high dark current; the cooling is what makes it usable. Field experience: in luminescence it is “just good enough to be bad.” No warm-up, stability or drift figure is published.

Synergy H1

One PMT per light path (one monochromator, one filter cube); photodiode for absorbance; red-shifted option to 900 nm. Two colors one after the other.

Saturates at 99,999 RFU.

Synergy Neo2

Up to three PMTs. The two top detectors are different types: one extended into the red, one lower-noise that “isn’t responsive above 700nm.” Bottom: one PMT. Simultaneous dual emission top only, Dual Filter Top builds only, and the cube for it is special order (“please contact BioTek”).

A simultaneous ratio compares readings from two different kinds of tube. BioTek’s own installation test allows the red-shifted tube ten times the luminescence detection limit of the low-noise one (≤500 vs ≤50 amol). Choose two blue tubes and TR-FRET suffers; two red and BRET is ruined; one of each and neither is good.

Tecan Spark

One fluorescence PMT, one photon-counting luminescence PMT, a photodiode for absorbance. Every two-color fluorescence ratio is two reads. NanoBRET: donor then acceptor, 300 ms each.

—
VANTAstar

One low-noise PMT; CCD spectrometer. Two colors read one after the other. No red-shifted option.

—
Varioskan LUX

One PMT for every mode. Two colors one after the other. Luminescence calibration includes a dark-level drift check and expires every 10 minutes.

—

10 Monochromator bandwidth, minimum and maximum

Bandwidth trades light for selectivity: wide for a dim dye, narrow to separate two close colors. The iD, the Varioskan (emission) and the standard Spark module have no bandwidth setting; the Neo2, the H1 M2 builds and the enhanced Spark stop at 50 nm.

Monochromator bandwidth, minimum and maximum
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

8–100 nm, continuously, in 1 nm steps, excitation and emission set separately.

Widest bandwidth published on any reader in this matrix. No slit: the band is the overlap of two linear variable filters.

EnVision Nexus

Not applicable: no monochromator. Bandwidth is whatever the fitted filter module carries.

—
PHERAstar FSX

Not applicable: no monochromator. Bandwidth is set by the filters in each optic module, chosen when the module is built.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Fixed: 15 nm excitation, 25 nm emission. No bandwidth setting.

—
Synergy H1

Fixed 16 nm on most builds, including the MF hybrid. 9–50 nm only on the four M2 part numbers.

Agilent’s own H1 page says variable bandwidth delivers “increased sensitivity and increased specificity,” so by Agilent’s account the 16 nm builds give up both.

Synergy Neo2

3–50 nm, “wavelength dependent,” 1 nm steps.

—
Tecan Spark

Standard: fixed 20 nm. Enhanced: 5–50 nm.

Tecan on its own standard module: the 20 nm band “allows detection of too much background signal” and gives “a decreased dynamic range.” Tecan on its own grating: light is “approximately proportional to the square of the slit width,” so narrowing the band costs light fast.

VANTAstar

8–100 nm (93 settings), excitation and emission.

From a comparison table sent to a customer; not printed on the spec page.

Varioskan LUX

Excitation 5 or 12 nm. Emission “permanently set to 12 nm and cannot be changed.” Excitation and emission must sit at least 17 nm apart (24 nm with both at 12).

GFP emits over ~30 nm; a 12 nm slit leaves most of that undetected. Not on the product page or brochure; it is in the SkanIt technical manual.

11 Monochromator design: how it selects color and how it blocks the wrong color

Stray light is lamp light that reaches the detector; it sets the background every dim sample has to beat. A grating leaks about one part in a thousand (Tecan’s own figure), which is why grating readers add a second grating or steer sensitive assays to filters.

Monochromator design: how it selects color and how it blocks the wrong color
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Two linear variable filter (LVF) slides per monochromator, no grating, no slit. Light outside the band must pass two overlapping filters.

Tecan’s 2023 sales slide said LVFs give “less defined peaks”; BMG’s answer is to show the spectral scans.

EnVision Nexus

Not applicable: filter modules only. The manual: “It is advisable to insert the filter module in position 1 in order to obtain the best results.”

The slots are not equal.

PHERAstar FSX

Not applicable. Filters on a free-air light path, no light guides.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Grating monochromator. Blocking: the only stray-light figure published is for absorbance, ≤0.05% at 260 nm and 280 nm; no out-of-band rejection figure is given for the fluorescence or luminescence monochromators. MD, 2004 (GEMINI line): “a considerable amount of lamp light is reflected into emission beam. Raw background is much higher than in cuvette.”

The iD3 guide (Table A-2, p. 106) gives the same absorbance figure; the newer iD5e guide and brochure list it at 230 nm and 280 nm. The 2004 deck predates the iD series; the geometry it describes is the same.

Synergy H1

Grating monochromators. Blocking figure: not published. The error table, on a monochromator read: “the luminescence probe may be picking up stray light. Try installing a plug in the filter cube.”

Stray light can reach the detector, and the fix is a part in the cube.

Synergy Neo2

Grating monochromator on its own light path; Agilent calls it a “quad monochromator.” Out-of-band blocking figure for the fluorescence path: not published. The only stray-light number Agilent prints is for absorbance: 0.03% at 230 nm.

A BioTek-era Neo2 brochure (undated, hosted by a Harvard core facility) says “Four holographic gratings are used to eliminate stray light” but its own spec table lists “Double grating monochromators (top/bottom)”; neither version gives an OD or percent rejection figure.

Tecan Spark

Grating monochromators (“QuadX”); Tecan’s guide says the fluorescence module uses “double monochromators.” Blocking: 10⁶ for a double monochromator (10³ for a single one), a generic figure with no Spark-specific measurement. Tecan on the single-monochromator 10³: “this blocking is often not sufficient” for fluorescence.

This is the Spark’s own guide (v2.2, p. 163), the same passage the matrix had quoted from the Infinite 200 manual; superscripts are flattened to “103” and “106” in the text layer, and the guide’s worked example (10.000 counts vs 10 counts) confirms 10³.

VANTAstar

LVF, no grating, no slit. BMG: LVFs “eliminate the stray light issues found in conventional monochromators.”

—
Varioskan LUX

Gratings and slits; light guides carry light to and from the well. Light is lost at four points (excitation slit, delivery optic, emission light guide, emission slit).

Thermo’s 17 nm minimum separation rule exists “to prevent any stray light from the excitation light from interfering with the emission light.”

12 Are fixed dichroic mirrors needed on the monochromator path?

A dichroic is the mirror that sends excitation down to the plate and lets emission back up; it works for one color band. Tecan says in print that the dichroic is where the sensitivity comes from, then ships one color of it. The readers with no dichroic on the monochromator path use a 50% mirror or none, and lose light. Only the LVD tracks the dye.

Are fixed dichroic mirrors needed on the monochromator path?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No. Linear Variable Dichroic, 340–740 nm (to 760 nm with the red-shifted PMT): the mirror slides to match whatever wavelength the user sets, on every read. Patented.

The mirror is matched to the dye at every setting, with nothing to buy or fit.

EnVision Nexus

Not applicable: no monochromator. Every wavelength is a filter module, and the module list is fixed (7 excitation wavelengths).

—
PHERAstar FSX

Not applicable. Every optic module carries its own dichroic matched to its colors.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No dichroic on the monochromator path. Nothing to swap, and nothing matched to the dye.

—
Synergy H1

The monochromator path has no dichroic. BioTek: “Dichroic mirrors provide better sensitivity than 50% mirrors, but they are dye-specific.”

The monochromator path gets none of that sensitivity; the cube does, one dye at a time.

Synergy Neo2

The monochromator path has no dichroic at all; dichroics sit in the filter cubes. No tunable dichroic anywhere in the reader.

—
Tecan Spark

Yes. Standard module: one dichroic, at 510 nm, plus a 50% mirror. Enhanced: 510, 560 and 625 nm built in. Five more (410, 430, 458, 593, 660 nm) are “user-selectable” parts shipped in “a metal box… (including Allen key for installation).”

Tecan: “Combining QuadX Monochromators with dichroic mirrors gives the Spark reader industry-leading sensitivity.” Away from the fitted colors the light goes through the 50% mirror, which PerkinElmer’s manual says collects “only 25% of the possible emission signal.” The fluorescein spec is quoted at the one color the standard mirror sits at.

VANTAstar

No. Linear variable dichroic, 340–740 nm, tracks the wavelength on every read.

—
Varioskan LUX

No dichroic anywhere. Gratings, slits and light guides; no part of the path adjusts to the dye.

—

13 What a new dye color requires

What a new dye color requires
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

A new number in the software. Type the wavelengths in 1 nm steps or pick the dye by name; both LVF monochromators and the dichroic move to match.

—
EnVision Nexus

A new filter module, if Revvity makes one. 43 modules in the catalog; no custom modules. A pharma HTS site: “when they ask for a module for a new fluor they can’t get one.”

A protocol won’t start unless every module it names is loaded.

PHERAstar FSX

An optic module built for that color; “Any excitation and emission combination can be built to order.” Six positions, the sixth usually reserved for luminescence, so five assay modules sit in the reader at once; swap by hand in seconds; bar-coded. Lead time: not published (BMG’s site says delivery depends on configuration).

BMG’s Optic Modules page speaks of “five module bays,” which matches the five free for assay modules.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD3: a software setting (monochromator only). iD5: a filter slide to buy, or the monochromator; standard kit is 350/60, 490/10, 616/10 plus polarizers; HTRF needs its own set.

—
Synergy H1

New filters fitted by hand into the one cube (6-week lead time for custom), or the monochromator at 10× less sensitivity. BioTek’s own guide recommends 28 cube combinations for its fluorescent-protein list, for a reader that holds one cube.

—
Synergy Neo2

A new filter cube, or the monochromator at 10× less sensitivity. Custom filters: “typical lead time of 6 weeks.” Every custom cube reads as ID 255: “It is the user’s responsibility to ensure that the correct custom filter cube is installed.”

—
Tecan Spark

Away from the fitted mirror colors: a 50% mirror and a quarter of the light at best, or a dichroic bought, stored and fitted by the user with an Allen key. A dye 10 nm away can mean a new part.

Someone in the lab keeps the mirror box, the Allen key and the record of which mirror is in.

VANTAstar

A software setting. Filters: four excitation and four emission in slides; more by quote.

—
Varioskan LUX

Fluorescence: a software setting, through the fixed 12 nm slit. Luminescence, BRET, Alpha, TRF: an emission filter bought separately and fitted with a pick-up tool inside the LAT module.

—

14 Different filters or modules needed for top and bottom measurements?

Different filters or modules needed for top and bottom measurements?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No. Top or bottom is picked in software; autofocus to 0.1 mm on both sides. Bottom reading is a module.

—
EnVision Nexus

Top and bottom for FI, TRF and standard luminescence. Top only: FP, Enhanced and Ultra-sensitive luminescence, both Alpha modes. In aperture modes the measurement height can’t be adjusted.

—
PHERAstar FSX

No. The same optic module reads top or bottom, in every mode including luminescence and Alpha; switch in software; autofocus.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No (software switch). Bottom luminescence is a factory-installed option at 300/400 pM against 10/20 pM from the top (30× and 20× weaker, calculated).

—
Synergy H1

Yes, in effect: filters read top only, so a bottom read means switching to the monochromator path. FP can’t be read from the bottom at all.

—
Synergy Neo2

Yes. The cube that reads from the top does not read from the bottom: “Users may need to purchase two GFP modules.” One bottom cube fits at a time. Fixed bottom focus. Luminescence reads from the top only. Nothing two-color possible from the bottom.

No BRET, GeneBLAzer or any two-color read from the bottom, where most cell assays want to be read.

Tecan Spark

No for fluorescence (software switch, auto Z-focus both sides). Luminescence from the bottom: not confirmed in Tecan’s manual.

—
VANTAstar

No. Automatic switching, no hardware to move; autofocus 0.1 mm; FP, luminescence and TR-FRET all read from the bottom.

—
Varioskan LUX

No; switched in software. No focus adjustment from either side; the plate adapter sets the height. Bottom luminescence not offered.

—

15 Maximum number of dual-emission assays resident before a physical module change

A reader that holds one assay’s optics at a time turns every assay switch into a hardware step, which is hard to automate and easy to get wrong.

Maximum number of dual-emission assays resident before a physical module change
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Unlimited on the monochromator path (software). Filter slides are software-identified; the excitation and emission slides each hold 4 filters.

BMG's CLARIOstar Plus spec page says the same twice: “Ex and em slides hold 4 filters each” and “Excitation and emission slides for 4 filters each”. The page does not say how many dual-emission pairs that allows.

EnVision Nexus

Six filter-module positions (Kaleido numbers them 1-6). Dual-channel filter modules read both colors at once; the Ultra-sensitive module reads one color.

MD’s LM1 validation plate checks 2.5–3 decades of luminescence on multimode readers and skips the dim rungs as “too dim to measure,” so the 7-decade claim is never re-checked on the customer’s unit. Three SpectraTest plates, one per mode: “it must be returned to Molecular Devices. Only Molecular Devices has the necessary knowledge and equipment to recertify”; yearly; book a month ahead. Repair is at MD’s depot: “Instruments not covered by Warranty or Service Plan are not eligible for a loaner.”

MD “is not liable for damage incurred during shipment.”

Synergy H1

OQ yearly; PQ monthly or quarterly. The absorbance test plate is recertified annually by BioTek; FP and TRF tests need a dedicated qualification cube. Lamp “not user-changeable.”

—
Synergy Neo2

Terms: the manual recommends the OQ “initially (before first use)” and then annually, and absorbance test plates are recertified by BioTek annually; warranty terms ship as a separate document and no length is printed in the manual. The luminescence OQ is one point at one gain, so the “>6 decades” is never re-checked on the customer’s unit. Wear to plan for: 768 cube moves per 384-well Alpha plate, an injector module needing a daily flush and overnight soak, and two xenon lamps “(not user-changeable).” Daily flushing is a warranty matter: “Failure to follow preventive maintenance protocols may void the warranty.”

Agilent’s US Terms of Sale (Apr 2024) say only that “Each Product receives a global warranty which includes the standard warranty for the country of purchase” and refer to a separate warranty page; the instrument warranty length was not found.

Tecan Spark

Tecan lists “QC tools for IQOQ services”: the MultiCheck Plus QC plate, which Tecan recalibrates at its factory annually. The guide calls for an annual maintenance procedure by a Tecan service engineer. Te-Care contracts list a loaner only as a billed option (footnote: “Subject to availability”); the 48-hour onsite response is in COMPLETE only.

Te-Care and QC-plate terms are from Tecan’s web pages (tecan.com/service-contracts, Detection & Others tab; lifesciences.tecan.com/microplate-readers-qc-tools); regional differences apply.

VANTAstar

Evaluation Plate sold as an accessory (NIST-traceable absorbance filters plus solid fluorescence and luminescence standards). BMG US service plans: Standard Depot includes a yearly QCPM; only Preferred Onsite includes a loaner. Repair turnaround: not published.

Same US service plans as the CLARIOstar Plus.

Varioskan LUX

Verification plates: spectrophotometric (N03394) and Lumiwell luminescence (2806460), plus a “Microplate package for Varioskan LUX IQ/OQ” (SP-00720). Warranty and service-plan terms for the LUX are not published. Thermo's Part 11 table puts validation and user training on the customer.

Thermo's generic Unity Lab Services plan page does not name the Varioskan or plate readers, and the Dana-Farber quote's “2Y WARR” is a customer quote, not a published term.

61 Support lifetime and end-of-service history

Support lifetime and end-of-service history
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

By BMG’s own account, no BMG reader has ever been phased out of service support.

—
EnVision Nexus

One Windows build for the life of the PC: Windows 10 IoT LTSC 2021, “No, the license is only valid exactly for” that version, supported to January 2032. Kaleido upgrades run one way (4.0 data into 4.1, “but not vice versa”). Revvity publishes no instrument end-of-support policy for the Nexus.

Revvity's service terms reserve the right to refuse a repair order for instrument obsolescence or parts availability, but set no minimum support period.

PHERAstar FSX

“Any 16-bit unit will have a guaranteed 10 years of support from the point of purchase.” No BMG reader phased out of support.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not published. MD’s repair FAQ states no obsolescence policy.

—
Synergy H1

No end-of-service date found for the H1 (on sale since 2010). Sibling Synergy Mx: discontinued 2015, service ended Oct 1, 2022 (BioTek’s 2021 notice). H4, Synergy 2 and HT no longer sold or supported.

—
Synergy Neo2

Agilent’s published Service Terms let it drop a product from service coverage on 60 days’ written notice; no Neo2-specific support-life period is published. Support for the sibling Synergy Mx ended ~5.5 years after one account’s purchase. Labs are replacing BioTek readers that BioTek stopped supporting (field experience).

The clause governs service agreements and sets a notice period, not a minimum support life; the Neo2 manual, data sheet and product page state no support-life commitment.

Tecan Spark

Tecan’s own schedule: Infinite M1000 shipped to March 2012, support ended March 2019: “no sales, no service packs, no modifications (we expect customers to upgrade in case of problems).” About seven years from sale. The Spark is based on the M1000 (user reports).

Tecan has since removed the schedule from its website; an archived copy exists.

VANTAstar

“Free tech and application support for the lifetime of the reader” (BMG value sheet).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not published. Thermo gives no support-lifetime or end-of-service policy for the LUX. The Varioskan Flash page is marked discontinued and points to the LUX, with no end-of-service date.

62 Relocation: what moving the reader down the hall involves

Relocation: what moving the reader down the hall involves
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No restriction. 32 kg, two people.

—
EnVision Nexus

“Allow the instrument to acclimatize for at least 24 hours after shipping or transport.” Stacker removal “may only be carried out by a Revvity service engineer.” 90 kg; 100 kg with stacker. “Sensitive to vibrations.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

Nothing extra to disconnect; AAS has no external vents or plumbing.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Moving terms: a customer procedure (guide p. 125) that does not call for a Molecular Devices engineer: remove filter slides and any Enhanced TRF module, touch “Lock Instrument,” fit the transport locks, lift with at least two people. “The instrument can be damaged if the transport locks are not removed before the instrument is powered on.” 40 kg. Original packaging is called for only to store, ship or move it to another building, and warranty claims are void if transport damage is caused by improper packing.

The iD3 guide carries the same procedure (p. 98); the iD5e guide renames the touchscreen step “Prepare Shipment - Lock Instrument.”

Synergy H1

Shipping brackets must go back in, in original packaging “designed to be used no more than five times.” Shipping any other way “can void the warranty.”

—
Synergy Neo2

No restriction found in the manual.

—
Tecan Spark

“Do not ship an instrument with integrated cooling module! Only Tecan authorized service technicians are allowed to prepare instrument for transportation. Residual cooling fluid might damage the instrument.”

Moving a Te-Cool Spark starts with a service call; a field note: versions you can’t move yourself without voiding the warranty.

VANTAstar

No restriction found. 27 kg.

—
Varioskan LUX

Refit the tray-holder transport lock before moving it (front cover off, four screws, ten steps), keep the original packaging, and plan a two-person lift at 53-60 kg. Thermo also offers a service to move the instrument.

The manuals give 53-60 kg (the product page lists 57 kg), not 54-59 kg, and do not say whether the per-unit luminescence alignment must be repeated after a move.

64 Field accounts and public reviews (reported, not independently established)

Reported accounts, not independent tests. Use these accounts to identify questions for further investigation.

Field accounts and public reviews (reported, not independently established)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

SelectScience: five stars, two years after launch (2021).

—
EnVision Nexus

A pharma HTS site with two Nexus readers “no one is using”: modules unobtainable, PC off the domain, exports breaking LIMS. A biotech called its demo “a disaster” (broke twice, missing accessories). 2023 pharma demo: “our unit laser was broken.” A pharma BRET comparison: “certainly the Nexus was not better.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

1536 LanthaScreen (2013): matched a competing HTS reader’s 15-minute assay quality in 6 minutes, with a 40% larger window. Customers at a 2023 show said a competitor’s new flagship looked like a copy of it.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

SelectScience iD3 page (April 2025): 3.2 / 5 from six reviews, featured quote “Don’t buy this one.” A university iD3’s built-in computer failed twice on the same part just past warranty; MD would not cover it; the group bought another make. r/labrats: two MD units returned for refund in ten years.

MD’s tagline on the same page: “Unparalleled performance on a personalized platform.”

Synergy H1

A core facility’s handwritten sign: “Please measure nano orange and mCherry plates with filter cubes, not with the monochromator!” In 2026 an Agilent rep sent a customer an AI-drafted comparison labeled a “3rd party Competitive review.”

That comparison gives the H1MF “~7 logs” and concedes the competing BMG reader “up to ~8 logs.”

Synergy Neo2

Almost no high-volume Alpha labs (field experience ties it to the 768-move design). NanoBRET, 2018: “Can’t do it from the bottom.” Caution: in a 2013 top-read TR-FRET demo the original Neo held its own.

—
Tecan Spark

A San Diego biotech’s new Spark couldn’t read its assays; service couldn’t fix it; the replacement failed the same way; they switched makes, and the director will take calls. A 2024 European demo: “The Spark… was slow and had bad performance for this plate.”

—
VANTAstar

SelectScience: 4.8 of 5, five reviews, 2023–2025.

—
Varioskan LUX

A genomics lab’s own PicoGreen QC test at matched 45 µL: signal over background 14.5, 5.2 and 15.2 against 32.9, 29.7 and 31.8 on the reader the lab bought; the lab put the Varioskan above its 20% CV limit. Slide: “Varioskan does not like Picogreen at low conc.”

A 2022 competitive view: “They haven’t released a new reader in years.”

blocks.html:
3 Fluorescence sensitivity, top, filters (fluorescein, converted to pM where the vendor gives a volume)

Filters are the sensitive path on every reader that has both. The number to compare is pM in a stated plate and volume; three vendors here print per-well amounts with no volume, or two different volumes on one sheet.

Fluorescence sensitivity, top, filters (fluorescein, converted to pM where the vendor gives a volume)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<0.15 pM / <3 amol (384 small-volume, 20 µL).

—
EnVision Nexus

<2 pM (module 1001, 485/535 nm; 50 µL, 384 OptiPlate) = 100 amol; a comparison sheet gives 200 amol. Flash count not stated.

Excitation exists at 340, 355, 400, 485, 535, 555 and 632 nm only. A dye in between has no module. The filter-module list is sparse.

PHERAstar FSX

<0.15 pM / <3 amol (384sv black, 20 µL). 1536: <0.5 pM (8 µL).

Free-air light path: lenses, no fiber bundles.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD5 only: 3 pM guaranteed, 0.5 pM optimized (384; volume not stated). iD3: no filters.

The iD3 has no filter path at all; every iD3 fluorescence read is a monochromator read.

Synergy H1

0.25 pM / 25 amol (384, works out to 100 µL). Manual guarantee: ≤10 pM (96-well; 3 pM typical in the IFU).

Filters read from the top only. The sheet figure is 40× better than the guarantee.

Synergy Neo2

0.2 pM / 4 amol (384 low-volume, 20 µL), typical. 1536: 1 pM (10 µL). BioTek’s brochure calls these “the average observed factory test values”; the 2016 manual (Appendix A) guarantees <5 pM filters and ≤20 pM monochromator, 25× and 10× the averages.

Sensitivity is qualified at Normal speed with 50 measurements per point; the 11 s sweep-mode speed on the same sheet comes from a different setting.

Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤25 amol in 100 µL = 0.25 pM. Enhanced: ≤8 amol in 10 µL (1536) = 0.8 pM. Calculated.

Quoted at fluorescein, the one color the standard module’s single 510 nm dichroic sits at. The manual’s binding spec for the standard module is <10 pM (40× the brochure).

VANTAstar

<0.5 pM / <10 amol (384sv, 20 µL).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not offered. Fluorescence intensity is monochromator only; the Varioskan’s filters serve luminescence, Alpha, BRET and TRF.

There is no filter path to fall back on when a fluorescence assay needs more light.

4 Fluorescence sensitivity, bottom, filters

Cell-based assays in clear-bottom plates are read from the bottom. Ask early whether the assay is read from the top or the bottom: on the Neo2 that exposes a build dependency, on the H1 it exposes the monochromator, on the Nexus three modes don’t read from below at all.

Fluorescence sensitivity, bottom, filters
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<1.0 pM / <50 amol (384 glass-bottom, 50 µL).

—
EnVision Nexus

Not published. Bottom FI is offered; the spec sheet gives no figure. “On-the-fly mode is not available when measuring from below.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

<1.0 pM (384g black, 50 µL). Same optic module reads top or bottom; autofocus.

From the bottom it still reads both emission colors at once, plus luminescence and Alpha.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not published for filters; the published bottom figure is the monochromator one (2.5 pM optimized).

Read height “should be optimized for each new lot of microplates or assay volume used.”

Synergy H1

Not offered. Filters read top only; every bottom read is a monochromator read.

—
Synergy Neo2

1 pM (100 µL, 384). Fixed bottom focus. Bottom reads need their own cubes and exist only on dual-top-PMT builds.

BioTek’s 2012 guide: bottom sensitivity “not demonstrated.” One bottom detector, so no simultaneous dual emission from below.

Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤500 amol (100 µL) = 5 pM. Enhanced: ≤180 amol (10 µL) = 18 pM. Calculated.

Twenty times the top figure on the same sheet.

VANTAstar

<2.5 pM / <125 amol (384g, 50 µL).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not offered (no filter FI).

—

blocks.html:
5 Fluorescence sensitivity, top, monochromator

On every sheet here that prints both, the monochromator is less sensitive than the filters. The size of the loss differs: ~2× on the BMG readers, 2.6× on the Spark by Tecan’s own note, 10× on the Neo2 and H1 by Agilent’s own sheet.

Fluorescence sensitivity, top, monochromator
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<0.35 pM / <7 amol (384sv, 20 µL). Best monochromator figure published on any reader in this matrix.

The monochromator is about 2× less sensitive than the filters on the same sheet; the other readers lose 2× to 10×.

EnVision Nexus

Not offered. No monochromator in any mode.

—
PHERAstar FSX

No monochromator. Filter optic modules only.

Built for screening: every assay reads through a module made for its colors.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

6 pM guaranteed, 1 pM optimized (384; volume not stated). The iD3’s only fluorescence path.

MD’s own brochure rates its filters “10–40 times more sensitive than conventional monochromator based detection” in the near-IR. The iD3 has no filters.

Synergy H1

2.5 pM / 250 amol (384, 100 µL): 10× worse than its own filters. Manual guarantee ≤20 pM (96-well).

Fixed 16 nm band on most builds. A core facility taped a sign above its Synergy: “Please measure nano orange and mCherry plates with filter cubes, not with the monochromator!”

Synergy Neo2

2 pM / 40 amol (384 low-volume, 20 µL): ten times less sensitive than its own filters.

BioTek’s 2012 newsletter: “Filters are more optically efficient and will give you the best performance.”

Tecan Spark

Standard: ≤50 amol (100 µL) = 0.5 pM. Enhanced: ≤20 amol (10 µL) = 2 pM. Manual spec for the standard module: <20 pM.

Tecan’s own tech note prices its monochromator at 1.5–1.7× on one arm and 2.6× on both and calls that “comparable results.” The brochure figure uses the 510 nm dichroic; a dye away from fluorescein reads through a 50% mirror.

VANTAstar

<0.8 pM / <16 amol (384sv, 20 µL).

Under twice the filter figure (calculated).

Varioskan LUX

<400 amol per well (black 384; volume not stated) = 4 pM at 100 µL or 20 pM at 20 µL (calculated for both).

Its only fluorescence path, through an emission slit fixed at 12 nm. In a lab’s own PicoGreen QC test it failed the lab’s 20% CV limit; a fluorescein series across 3–400 amol read flat on it.

7 Practical fluorescence dynamic range in one gain setting, without re-reading the plate

Take a plate whose brightest and dimmest wells are a million-fold apart. Readers that pick a gain per well inside the read see both at once; readers that fix a gain per read see one end and clip or lose the other, and the fix is a second pass. The Spark and Neo2 can widen effective range by reading the plate twice; that doubles the read time and breaks kinetic timing.

Practical fluorescence dynamic range in one gain setting, without re-reading the plate
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

8 decades in a single measurement (Enhanced Dynamic Range): a test flash picks a factory-calibrated gain per well, inside the delay the read already has.

Works in kinetics, with injectors and with a stacker. The user never sets a gain. Flying mode, the fastest read, runs at a fixed gain without EDR; in standard mode EDR’s test flash fits inside the pause the read already takes.

EnVision Nexus

No gain to set on the Ultra-sensitive photon counter and no published count-rate ceiling. Filter-path PMTs: no gain setting in any Kaleido 4.1 operation; the only bright-sample control it names is an “Attenuated” filter-module property.

None of the ten operation parameter lists in the Kaleido 4.1 manual (Rev E) has a gain, PMT-voltage or sensitivity entry, and the 2026 filter list (2321302) shows no module marked attenuated.

PHERAstar FSX

8 decades in one visit to the well (EDR). 700,000,000 counts.

Works in kinetics and with a stacker. Flying mode, the fastest read, runs at a fixed gain without EDR; in standard mode EDR’s test flash fits inside the pause the read already takes.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Kinetics run at a fixed gain chosen before the run, “a nominal dynamic range of three decades” per gain (MD, 2026). Endpoints get AutoPMT: a pre-read at High, then re-reads of saturated wells at Medium and Low.

MD’s own Figure 3: High saturates at 33 nM, Medium at 333 nM, Low is “losing sensitivity at low concentration.” The iD5 widens range for endpoints by re-reading saturated wells and, in fluorescence, by adjusting lamp intensity; it can’t do that in a kinetic or in luminescence. “For kinetic read, the PMT settings have to be fixed”; each gain covers “a nominal dynamic range of three decades.”

Synergy H1

A single read tops out at 99,999 RFU; the manual’s remedy for saturation is “Try lowering the gain/sensitivity” (read again). BioTek’s 2010 table gave 5 decades; the 2026 sheet says 7 for the same model.

Gain is set per read, by number or scaled to a well the user picks as brightest.

Synergy Neo2

Fixed gain per read, ceiling 10 million counts. “Auto-ranging” runs a gain check on every well and adds minutes per plate. BioTek support: use manual gain “for kinetic tests, rapid reads or for tests that require high sensitivity.”

Extended range by re-reading is possible for endpoints; for flash luminescence BioTek’s own tips say it is “simply not possible.”

Tecan Spark

One gain, chosen before the read, about 3–4 decades usable (inferred from Tecan’s help text). Tecan’s “extended dynamic range” is “Two consecutive measurement runs with a high and a low amplification” with the listed drawback “Long measurement times.”

Every one of Tecan’s four gain modes has a printed “Disadvantages” panel. Optimal mode: “If signal intensities within one plate are very far spread, certain signals might not be detected any more.” Two passes means the same well is read twice, at two moments; a kinetic can’t hold its timing. The two-pass method does widen the effective range for endpoints. Extended range is “Two consecutive measurement runs”; its listed drawback: “Long measurement times.”

VANTAstar

8 decades in a single measurement (EDR), gain set per well in <0.1 s.

—
Varioskan LUX

Auto gain picks one of four calibrated gains per well from a trial flash. Product page commits to FI >6 decades; the tech note shows seven.

Whether auto gain runs in kinetic reads: not published. The gain is chosen before the signal moves.

8 Who sets the detector gain, and when

When the user sets the gain before the read, a plate brighter or dimmer than expected has to be read again, and the time points of a kinetic run cannot be read again.

Who sets the detector gain, and when
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Nobody. EDR picks a calibrated gain per well from a test flash. Manual gain is available.

—
EnVision Nexus

No gain on Ultra-sensitive luminescence or HT Alpha (“Only one detector”). Filter path: no gain setting in any of the ten Kaleido 4.1 measurement operations.

Revvity does not say in words whether the filter-path PMT gain is fixed or automatic inside the instrument; Kaleido offers no control, and the “Attenuated” filter-module property is its only bright-sample lever.

PHERAstar FSX

Nobody on current units (EDR). Flying mode runs at a fixed gain.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

The user, before a kinetic (“the PMT settings have to be fixed”); AutoPMT for endpoints only. Two wavelengths lock the gain at High.

The “gain locked at High for multiple-wavelength reads” sentence comes from the SoftMax Pro 7.0.2 guide for the i3x; no iD guide confirms it yet.

Synergy H1

The user, per read: a number, or scaled to the well the user picks as brightest.

—
Synergy Neo2

The user, per read, or auto-ranging per well at a time cost.

—
Tecan Spark

The user, before the read, from four modes (manual, calculated from well, optimal, extended). Each mode has a printed disadvantage.

Optimal: “Signals between different runs might not be comparable.” Calculated from well: “If any signal intensities from another well are higher, the detector might be oversaturated.”

VANTAstar

Nobody (EDR).

—
Varioskan LUX

The reader, one of four gains from a trial flash before each well; kinetic behavior not published.

—

9 Detectors: how many, what kind, and whether two colors can be read at the same instant

Simultaneous dual emission means the two halves of a ratio come from the same flash, so lamp flicker and timing drop out of the ratio. Only two readers here do it as standard, and only one does it on identical detectors and from the bottom.

Detectors: how many, what kind, and whether two colors can be read at the same instant
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

One low-noise PMT; red-shifted PMT option to 900 nm; CCD spectrometer for absorbance. Two colors read one after the other.

—
EnVision Nexus

Two PMTs on the filter path (230–850 nm), simultaneous dual channel via dual-channel module. One PMT, 400–650 nm, on the Ultra-sensitive/HT-Alpha module, no filters. Photodiode for absorbance.

The most sensitive mode is one detector, one color, top only. BRET and any two-color luminescence drop to a less sensitive rung. The single-PMT “Nexus One” (2026) has no simultaneous pair at all.

PHERAstar FSX

Two matched pairs of PMTs (low-noise pair for FI/FP/lum; red-shifted pair for TR-FRET) plus a CCD spectrometer. Both channels of any ratio read at the same instant, top or bottom.

Simultaneous dual emission in FI, FP, luminescence, TR-FRET and Alpha, from the same flash, on identical detectors.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

One “ultra-cooled” PMT for every mode, emission to 850 nm. Two colors one after the other. Photocathode type not named.

A tube that reaches 850 nm is red-extended and carries high dark current; the cooling is what makes it usable. Field experience: in luminescence it is “just good enough to be bad.” No warm-up, stability or drift figure is published.

Synergy H1

One PMT per light path (one monochromator, one filter cube); photodiode for absorbance; red-shifted option to 900 nm. Two colors one after the other.

Saturates at 99,999 RFU.

Synergy Neo2

Up to three PMTs. The two top detectors are different types: one extended into the red, one lower-noise that “isn’t responsive above 700nm.” Bottom: one PMT. Simultaneous dual emission top only, Dual Filter Top builds only, and the cube for it is special order (“please contact BioTek”).

A simultaneous ratio compares readings from two different kinds of tube. BioTek’s own installation test allows the red-shifted tube ten times the luminescence detection limit of the low-noise one (≤500 vs ≤50 amol). Choose two blue tubes and TR-FRET suffers; two red and BRET is ruined; one of each and neither is good.

Tecan Spark

One fluorescence PMT, one photon-counting luminescence PMT, a photodiode for absorbance. Every two-color fluorescence ratio is two reads. NanoBRET: donor then acceptor, 300 ms each.

—
VANTAstar

One low-noise PMT; CCD spectrometer. Two colors read one after the other. No red-shifted option.

—
Varioskan LUX

One PMT for every mode. Two colors one after the other. Luminescence calibration includes a dark-level drift check and expires every 10 minutes.

—

No slit: the band is the overlap of two linear variable filters. | EnVision Nexus | Not applicable: no monochromator. Bandwidth is whatever the fitted filter module carries. | — | PHERAstar FSX | Not applicable: no monochromator. 10 Monochromator bandwidth, minimum and maximum

Bandwidth trades light for selectivity: wide for a dim dye, narrow to separate two close colors. The iD, the Varioskan (emission) and the standard Spark module have no bandwidth setting; the Neo2, the H1 M2 builds and the enhanced Spark stop at 50 nm.

Monochromator bandwidth, minimum and maximum
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

8–100 nm, continuously, in 1 nm steps, excitation and emission set separately.

Widest bandwidth published on any reader in this matrix. No slit: the band is the overlap of two linear variable filters.

EnVision Nexus

Not applicable: no monochromator. Bandwidth is whatever the fitted filter module carries.

—
PHERAstar FSX

Not applicable: no monochromator. Bandwidth is set by the filters in each optic module, chosen when the module is built.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Fixed: 15 nm excitation, 25 nm emission. No bandwidth setting.

—
Synergy H1

Fixed 16 nm on most builds, including the MF hybrid. 9–50 nm only on the four M2 part numbers.

Agilent’s own H1 page says variable bandwidth delivers “increased sensitivity and increased specificity,” so by Agilent’s account the 16 nm builds give up both.

Synergy Neo2

3–50 nm, “wavelength dependent,” 1 nm steps.

—
Tecan Spark

Standard: fixed 20 nm. Enhanced: 5–50 nm.

Tecan on its own standard module: the 20 nm band “allows detection of too much background signal” and gives “a decreased dynamic range.” Tecan on its own grating: light is “approximately proportional to the square of the slit width,” so narrowing the band costs light fast.

VANTAstar

8–100 nm (93 settings), excitation and emission.

From a comparison table sent to a customer; not printed on the spec page.

Varioskan LUX

Excitation 5 or 12 nm. Emission “permanently set to 12 nm and cannot be changed.” Excitation and emission must sit at least 17 nm apart (24 nm with both at 12).

GFP emits over ~30 nm; a 12 nm slit leaves most of that undetected. Not on the product page or brochure; it is in the SkanIt technical manual.

11 Monochromator design: how it selects color and how it blocks the wrong color

Stray light is lamp light that reaches the detector; it sets the background every dim sample has to beat. A grating leaks about one part in a thousand (Tecan’s own figure), which is why grating readers add a second grating or steer sensitive assays to filters.

Monochromator design: how it selects color and how it blocks the wrong color
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Two linear variable filter (LVF) slides per monochromator, no grating, no slit. Light outside the band must pass two overlapping filters.

Tecan’s 2023 sales slide said LVFs give “less defined peaks”; BMG’s answer is to show the spectral scans.

EnVision Nexus

Not applicable: filter modules only. The manual: “It is advisable to insert the filter module in position 1 in order to obtain the best results.”

The slots are not equal.

PHERAstar FSX

Not applicable. Filters on a free-air light path, no light guides.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Grating monochromator. Blocking: the only stray-light figure published is for absorbance, ≤0.05% at 260 nm and 280 nm; no out-of-band rejection figure is given for the fluorescence or luminescence monochromators. MD, 2004 (GEMINI line): “a considerable amount of lamp light is reflected into emission beam. Raw background is much higher than in cuvette.”

The iD3 guide (Table A-2, p. 106) gives the same absorbance figure; the newer iD5e guide and brochure list it at 230 nm and 280 nm. The 2004 deck predates the iD series; the geometry it describes is the same.

Synergy H1

Grating monochromators. Blocking figure: not published. The error table, on a monochromator read: “the luminescence probe may be picking up stray light. Try installing a plug in the filter cube.”

Stray light can reach the detector, and the fix is a part in the cube.

Synergy Neo2

Grating monochromator on its own light path; Agilent calls it a “quad monochromator.” Out-of-band blocking figure for the fluorescence path: not published. The only stray-light number Agilent prints is for absorbance: 0.03% at 230 nm.

A BioTek-era Neo2 brochure (undated, hosted by a Harvard core facility) says “Four holographic gratings are used to eliminate stray light” but its own spec table lists “Double grating monochromators (top/bottom)”; neither version gives an OD or percent rejection figure.

Tecan Spark

Grating monochromators (“QuadX”); Tecan’s guide says the fluorescence module uses “double monochromators.” Blocking: 10⁶ for a double monochromator (10³ for a single one), a generic figure with no Spark-specific measurement. Tecan on the single-monochromator 10³: “this blocking is often not sufficient” for fluorescence.

This is the Spark’s own guide (v2.2, p. 163), the same passage the matrix had quoted from the Infinite 200 manual; superscripts are flattened to “103” and “106” in the text layer, and the guide’s worked example (10.000 counts vs 10 counts) confirms 10³.

VANTAstar

LVF, no grating, no slit. BMG: LVFs “eliminate the stray light issues found in conventional monochromators.”

—
Varioskan LUX

Gratings and slits; light guides carry light to and from the well. Light is lost at four points (excitation slit, delivery optic, emission light guide, emission slit).

Thermo’s 17 nm minimum separation rule exists “to prevent any stray light from the excitation light from interfering with the emission light.”

12 Are fixed dichroic mirrors needed on the monochromator path?

A dichroic is the mirror that sends excitation down to the plate and lets emission back up; it works for one color band. Tecan says in print that the dichroic is where the sensitivity comes from, then ships one color of it. The readers with no dichroic on the monochromator path use a 50% mirror or none, and lose light. Only the LVD tracks the dye.

Are fixed dichroic mirrors needed on the monochromator path?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No. Linear Variable Dichroic, 340–740 nm (to 760 nm with the red-shifted PMT): the mirror slides to match whatever wavelength the user sets, on every read. Patented.

The mirror is matched to the dye at every setting, with nothing to buy or fit.

EnVision Nexus

Not applicable: no monochromator. Every wavelength is a filter module, and the module list is fixed (7 excitation wavelengths).

—
PHERAstar FSX

Not applicable. Every optic module carries its own dichroic matched to its colors.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No dichroic on the monochromator path. Nothing to swap, and nothing matched to the dye.

—
Synergy H1

The monochromator path has no dichroic. BioTek: “Dichroic mirrors provide better sensitivity than 50% mirrors, but they are dye-specific.”

The monochromator path gets none of that sensitivity; the cube does, one dye at a time.

Synergy Neo2

The monochromator path has no dichroic at all; dichroics sit in the filter cubes. No tunable dichroic anywhere in the reader.

—
Tecan Spark

Yes. Standard module: one dichroic, at 510 nm, plus a 50% mirror. Enhanced: 510, 560 and 625 nm built in. Five more (410, 430, 458, 593, 660 nm) are “user-selectable” parts shipped in “a metal box… (including Allen key for installation).”

Tecan: “Combining QuadX Monochromators with dichroic mirrors gives the Spark reader industry-leading sensitivity.” Away from the fitted colors the light goes through the 50% mirror, which PerkinElmer’s manual says collects “only 25% of the possible emission signal.” The fluorescein spec is quoted at the one color the standard mirror sits at.

VANTAstar

No. Linear variable dichroic, 340–740 nm, tracks the wavelength on every read.

—
Varioskan LUX

No dichroic anywhere. Gratings, slits and light guides; no part of the path adjusts to the dye.

—

13 What a new dye color requires

What a new dye color requires
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

A new number in the software. Type the wavelengths in 1 nm steps or pick the dye by name; both LVF monochromators and the dichroic move to match.

—
EnVision Nexus

A new filter module, if Revvity makes one. 43 modules in the catalog; no custom modules. A pharma HTS site: “when they ask for a module for a new fluor they can’t get one.”

A protocol won’t start unless every module it names is loaded.

PHERAstar FSX

An optic module built for that color; “Any excitation and emission combination can be built to order.” Six positions, the sixth usually reserved for luminescence, so five assay modules sit in the reader at once; swap by hand in seconds; bar-coded. Lead time: not published (BMG’s site says delivery depends on configuration).

BMG’s Optic Modules page speaks of “five module bays,” which matches the five free for assay modules.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD3: a software setting (monochromator only). iD5: a filter slide to buy, or the monochromator; standard kit is 350/60, 490/10, 616/10 plus polarizers; HTRF needs its own set.

—
Synergy H1

New filters fitted by hand into the one cube (6-week lead time for custom), or the monochromator at 10× less sensitivity. BioTek’s own guide recommends 28 cube combinations for its fluorescent-protein list, for a reader that holds one cube.

—
Synergy Neo2

A new filter cube, or the monochromator at 10× less sensitivity. Custom filters: “typical lead time of 6 weeks.” Every custom cube reads as ID 255: “It is the user’s responsibility to ensure that the correct custom filter cube is installed.”

—
Tecan Spark

Away from the fitted mirror colors: a 50% mirror and a quarter of the light at best, or a dichroic bought, stored and fitted by the user with an Allen key. A dye 10 nm away can mean a new part.

Someone in the lab keeps the mirror box, the Allen key and the record of which mirror is in.

VANTAstar

A software setting. Filters: four excitation and four emission in slides; more by quote.

—
Varioskan LUX

Fluorescence: a software setting, through the fixed 12 nm slit. Luminescence, BRET, Alpha, TRF: an emission filter bought separately and fitted with a pick-up tool inside the LAT module.

—

14 Different filters or modules needed for top and bottom measurements?

Different filters or modules needed for top and bottom measurements?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No. Top or bottom is picked in software; autofocus to 0.1 mm on both sides. Bottom reading is a module.

—
EnVision Nexus

Top and bottom for FI, TRF and standard luminescence. Top only: FP, Enhanced and Ultra-sensitive luminescence, both Alpha modes. In aperture modes the measurement height can’t be adjusted.

—
PHERAstar FSX

No. The same optic module reads top or bottom, in every mode including luminescence and Alpha; switch in software; autofocus.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No (software switch). Bottom luminescence is a factory-installed option at 300/400 pM against 10/20 pM from the top (30× and 20× weaker, calculated).

—
Synergy H1

Yes, in effect: filters read top only, so a bottom read means switching to the monochromator path. FP can’t be read from the bottom at all.

—
Synergy Neo2

Yes. The cube that reads from the top does not read from the bottom: “Users may need to purchase two GFP modules.” One bottom cube fits at a time. Fixed bottom focus. Luminescence reads from the top only. Nothing two-color possible from the bottom.

No BRET, GeneBLAzer or any two-color read from the bottom, where most cell assays want to be read.

Tecan Spark

No for fluorescence (software switch, auto Z-focus both sides). Luminescence from the bottom: not confirmed in Tecan’s manual.

—
VANTAstar

No. Automatic switching, no hardware to move; autofocus 0.1 mm; FP, luminescence and TR-FRET all read from the bottom.

—
Varioskan LUX

No; switched in software. No focus adjustment from either side; the plate adapter sets the height. Bottom luminescence not offered.

—

15 Maximum number of dual-emission assays resident before a physical module change

A reader that holds one assay’s optics at a time turns every assay switch into a hardware step, which is hard to automate and easy to get wrong.

Maximum number of dual-emission assays resident before a physical module change
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Unlimited on the monochromator path (software). Filter slides are software-identified; the excitation and emission slides each hold 4 filters.

BMG's CLARIOstar Plus spec page says the same twice: “Ex and em slides hold 4 filters each” and “Excitation and emission slides for 4 filters each”. The page does not say how many dual-emission pairs that allows.

EnVision Nexus

Six filter-module positions (Kaleido numbers them 1-6). Dual-channel filter modules read both colors at once; the Ultra-sensitive module reads one color.

The six comes from Kaleido's “Position in Instrument” property; Revvity's spec sheet and flyers give no count.

PHERAstar FSX

Six optic modules in the reader at once (five included), one of them the luminescence module; each is one assay. Swap by hand in seconds, bar-coded.

Dual-emission is simultaneous on every one of them.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD5 filter slides, auto-ID; slot count per slide is not published. The guide says only that “The first slot on the tab end of the filter slide is always empty” and that a protocol can “define up to four wavelength pairs.” iD3: monochromator only (software). The Enhanced TRF module sits “on the transport slide”; what still fits beside it is not stated.

The Standard Filter Kit is listed as “seven filters and two filter slides,” which does not state slide capacity.

Synergy H1

One cube, two filter sets; an FP cube holds one set. Dual emission is sequential on one PMT. Swapping the whole cube is “the BioTek-recommended option.”

—
Synergy Neo2

One. Two cube slots on top; a dual-emission cube (FP, TR-FRET, Alpha) takes both, and the cube is special order. Changing assay means taking cubes out: Gen5 “prompt[s] for filter cube installation at runtime, if necessary.” Two cube slots, and an unattended run stops to ask for a cube. Many assays require both cube slots, so frequent manual changes are required. Not automation friendly.

An unattended run that needs another cube stops and waits for a person.

Tecan Spark

Mirror slide: 1 dichroic position (standard), 3 (enhanced); others user-fitted. Filter slides: 6 filter positions per slide, one excitation slide and one emission slide. Enhanced luminescence picks from 38 internal filters the user can’t choose.

Tecan cautions that “Any changes to the filters in the filter slide are to be carried out by trained personnel!”

VANTAstar

Unlimited on the monochromator path. Filters: 4 excitation + 4 emission in slides.

—
Varioskan LUX

Filter nest inside the LAT module with eight configurable filter positions (plus open and blocked). Each change is a five-step tool job. Dual emission sequential on one PMT.

Luminescence, AlphaScreen and TRF emission filters are customer-installed (p. 41), and the manual's filter table (Table 8-25, p. 99) lists no filters, only a referral to a sales representative.

18 Luminescence sensitivity, top (ATP; flash and glow are different tests)

These figures differ in kit and chemistry (glow vs flash), in whether a volume is given, and in whether they belong to an optional detector. The Neo2 and H1 data sheets name no volume or plate, so their headlines can’t be checked against the manuals’ 96-well guarantees. Revvity’s own technical note measured a Nexus detection limit 8,290× the spec sheet’s.

Luminescence sensitivity, top (ATP; flash and glow are different tests)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Flash: <0.4 pM / <8 amol ATP (384sv, 20 µL). Glow: <150 amol (comparison sheet).

Best flash figure published on any reader in this matrix (tied with the FSX).

EnVision Nexus

Spec sheet (ATPlite 1step, 384 AlphaPlate, 15 µL): Standard <0.25 pM, Enhanced <0.025 pM, Ultra-sensitive <0.001 pM. Revvity’s own technical note, same kit, plate and volume, 1 s integration: 138.77 / 85.99 / 8.29 pM.

The <0.001 pM figure implies detecting about one photon every 42 seconds, which is not physically achievable. Black 384 plates give a 4–5× worse LLOQ (Revvity’s own Table 2). The Ultra-sensitive mode is an option, one color, top only. Revvity’s own technical note measured its luminescence 8,290× worse than its spec sheet.

PHERAstar FSX

Flash: <0.4 pM / <8 amol ATP (384sv white, 20 µL). Dedicated luminescence optics on the low-noise PMT pair, top or bottom.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

10 pM (96) / 20 pM (384) guaranteed, ATPlite; live spec page prints 2 / 4 pM. The sensitive “All Wavelengths” setting covers 300–650 nm; no figure for the monochromator path.

One cooled red-reaching PMT does luminescence. Field experience: just good enough to be bad.

Synergy H1

Data sheet: 10 amol filters, 20 amol monochromator, no plate, no flash or glow stated. Manual guarantee: ≤75 amol/well, 96-well (30 typical); ≤500 amol with the red-shifted PMT.

The guarantee is 7.5× the sheet (calculated). BioTek’s own Gaussia note: “some additional signal variability… in the final three decades,” the dim end.

Synergy Neo2

Data sheet: 5 amol “typical” (384 low-volume; no read time, no detector named). Manual: “≤ 50 amol/well, 10 amol typical,” 96-well, 200 µL, 10 s per well. Installation pass line with the red-shifted tube: “≤ 500 amol.”

500 amol is 10× the manual’s spec, 50× the manual’s typical and 100× the data-sheet headline (different plate; calculated). Read through the cube’s “empty filter position,” with no aperture between plate and optics.

Tecan Spark

Glow ≤225 amol (25 µL, Biothema kit) = 9 pM. Flash ≤12 amol (55 µL, ENLITEN kit) = 0.22 pM. Calculated. Tecan’s Reference Guide specification: glow < 10 pM (384, 100 µL, 1 s per well); flash < 0.8 pM at 10 s per well (384, 100 µL).

Tecan’s own note on its warm chamber: glow signal +34% in six minutes at 4 °C above ambient, CV 7.7% against 0.3% at ambient. Tecan says the electronics warm the chamber by up to +4 °C. The guide’s flash figure is 3.7× the brochure’s 0.218 pM and needs 10 seconds per well: about an hour for a 384-well plate (calculated).

VANTAstar

<0.8 pM / <15 amol ATP (384sv, 20 µL).

—
Varioskan LUX

<7 amol ATP (white 384; assay and volume not published). Detects 360–670 nm.

Bottom luminescence not offered. Calibration expires every 10 minutes.

blocks.html:
20 Practical luminescence dynamic range in one gain setting

A photon counter with no gain is the most sensitive luminescence detector until the well gets bright. Then it misses photons, and unless the software corrects for it, the top of the curve flattens. Revvity publishes no correction or warning. Gain-per-well readers (EDR) cover the whole range in one read; fixed-gain readers cover ~3 decades per setting.

Practical luminescence dynamic range in one gain setting
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

8 decades in a single measurement (EDR), bright and dim wells on one plate without a second read.

—
EnVision Nexus

Revvity: “>8 logs” (Ultra-sensitive). No dead time, correction or overflow limit published. Analysis of a pharma customer’s paired plates found counting losses consistent with a ~48 ns dead time (about 20% at 5.4 million counts/s, before any correction).

Ask Revvity what Kaleido does about dead time and what appears when the detector’s over-light line goes high. Revvity documents no warning when high standards start to compress; in the customer’s plates, Z′ improved as signal was lost. The loss figures are before any dead-time correction. Past saturation, a counter’s reading falls as light rises, and no correction can recover that.

PHERAstar FSX

8 decades in one visit to the well (EDR). 200,000,000 counts

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

>7 decades as an endpoint figure (AutoPMT per well). Kinetics: a fixed gain, “a nominal dynamic range of three decades.” Low gain “requires Attenuation/Optical Density setting 0–3.”

The lamp-intensity trick that widens fluorescence range does not exist in luminescence.

Synergy H1

Not published in decades or counts. Gen5 marks overflow above 99,998 counts; in BioTek’s own luciferase note the operator set the gain by hand to stay “below the photomultiplier tube (PMT) saturation threshold (overflow).”

—
Synergy Neo2

Agilent: “> 6 decades.” With flash assays, extended range is “simply not possible” (BioTek’s own tips).

The Neo2 can widen effective range for glow endpoints by re-reading at a second gain.

Tecan Spark

>9 decades with gray attenuation filters (OD1–OD3; standard module OD1, OD2) chosen before the read. The enhanced module’s extra decade is the OD3 filter (inferred).

The Spark reaches those decades by picking a dimming filter before the read; the plate is still read at one gain. The Spark can also widen effective range by reading the plate twice.

VANTAstar

8 decades in a single measurement (EDR).

—
Varioskan LUX

>7 decades. Every luminescence calibration adds a dark-level check “to compensate for possible electronic component and photomultiplier signal level drift”; calibration expires every 10 minutes.

—

blocks.text: 22 Integrated crosstalk apertures (the mask between plate and detector that blocks neighboring wells)?Crosstalk is a bright well leaking into its neighbors. The mask has to sit between the plate and the lens; after the lens, it cannot block light the lens has already collected. Where the vendor’s own fix is “read every other well” or a smaller aperture that cuts signal, the aperture is not stopping the crosstalk.Integrated crosstalk apertures (the mask between plate and detector that blocks neighboring wells)?Reader | Specification or finding | Notes and conditions | CLARIOstar Plus | Yes. BMG’s application note AN371: an aperture spoon “is set up directly on top of the target well.” Crosstalk figure: not published on bmglabtech.com. | AN371 (2022) gives mathematical crosstalk-correction factors (white 0.05353%, gray 0.01277%, black 0.00026%), not an aperture crosstalk figure. | EnVision Nexus | Yes, but hand-swapped per plate format, in gloves, through a transfer plate and a wizard. 2023 manual: the match “is not validated by the software,” beside a legend reading “Does not produce reasonable data or even damages the instrument.” The 2024 warning can be dismissed: “You can ignore the warning and start the measurement in any case.” | A wrong aperture still produces a completed run. With an aperture in, the read height is fixed. Field notes: a mis-load can drop an aperture inside the instrument. | PHERAstar FSX | Yes: aperture spoons, one per plate format (96/384, 1536, 3456). The FSX manual offers them to “reduce crosstalk even further in certain applications.” Crosstalk figure: not published. | — | SpectraMax iD3 / iD5 | None described. Field reports: MD support “requests that customers use every other well when this is an issue,” which gives up half the plate. | — | Synergy H1 | None. No aperture is described anywhere in the H1 manual; luminescence reads through an empty cube position. | — | Synergy Neo2 | No aperture between the plate and the optics. The aperture sits inside the cube, after the collecting lens, where light from the neighbors has already been gathered (inferred). Crosstalk control is bought as “high sensitivity” and “low cross talk” cube variants. | Three BRET assays can mean six cubes. The “low cross talk” cube gives up much of the signal. | Tecan Spark | “Enhanced Aperture” is a separate line item. Figure: not published. | — | Varioskan LUX | A “crosstalk shield” after the light is collected, from one detection position.
