blocks.html:
22 Integrated crosstalk apertures (the mask between plate and detector that blocks neighboring wells)?

Crosstalk is a bright well leaking into its neighbors. The mask has to sit between the plate and the lens; after the lens, it cannot block light the lens has already collected. Where the vendor’s own fix is “read every other well” or a smaller aperture that cuts signal, the aperture is not stopping the crosstalk.

Integrated crosstalk apertures (the mask between plate and detector that blocks neighboring wells)?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Yes. BMG’s application note AN371: an aperture spoon “is set up directly on top of the target well.” Crosstalk figure: not published on bmglabtech.com.

AN371 (2022) gives mathematical crosstalk-correction factors (white 0.05353%, gray 0.01277%, black 0.00026%), not an aperture crosstalk figure.

EnVision Nexus

Yes, but hand-swapped per plate format, in gloves, through a transfer plate and a wizard. 2023 manual: the match “is not validated by the software,” beside a legend reading “Does not produce reasonable data or even damages the instrument.” The 2024 warning can be dismissed: “You can ignore the warning and start the measurement in any case.”

A wrong aperture still produces a completed run. With an aperture in, the read height is fixed. Field notes: a mis-load can drop an aperture inside the instrument.

PHERAstar FSX

Yes: aperture spoons, one per plate format (96/384, 1536, 3456). The FSX manual offers them to “reduce crosstalk even further in certain applications.” Crosstalk figure: not published.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

None described. Field reports: MD support “requests that customers use every other well when this is an issue,” which gives up half the plate.

—
Synergy H1

None. No aperture is described anywhere in the H1 manual; luminescence reads through an empty cube position.

—
Synergy Neo2

No aperture between the plate and the optics. The aperture sits inside the cube, after the collecting lens, where light from the neighbors has already been gathered (inferred). Crosstalk control is bought as “high sensitivity” and “low cross talk” cube variants.

Three BRET assays can mean six cubes. The “low cross talk” cube gives up much of the signal.

Tecan Spark

“Enhanced Aperture” is a separate line item. A 2023 university quote left it out.

—
VANTAstar

Yes, automatic: built-in luminescence crosstalk reduction, applied automatically up to 384 wells, no parts to place. Figure: not published.

—
Varioskan LUX

A “crosstalk shield” after the light is collected, from one detection position. Thermo’s remedies: a smaller aperture that works “by decreasing luminescense signals,” and re-aligning the LAT module after cleaning or service.

—

23 Published luminescence crosstalk figure

Promega published crosstalk data for the H1 (Figure 132), and Thermo published its own for the Varioskan (Figure 5). Neither vendor prints a crosstalk specification.

Published luminescence crosstalk figure
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Not published (brochure and spec page checked).

—
EnVision Nexus

Revvity’s figures are on its own AlphaPlates: “Most white plates show light leakage… This cannot be prevented by the optical design of a plate reader.” On White OptiPlate, Ultra-sensitive crosstalk was 0.70%, the worst of the three modes.

—
PHERAstar FSX

Not published on bmglabtech.com or in the FSX specification table.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

<0.1% in 96-well half-area, <0.2% in 384 small-volume, white Costar. Clear-bottom bottom reads: <0.4%.

Quoted in the easiest plates.

Synergy H1

Not published. Promega measured one H1 two ways, 96-well: 530 vs 5,063 RLU per 10⁶, depending on which mode the software was in first (9.6× apart).

Promega’s caption: “The same multimode reader produces differing well-to-well cross talk dependent upon instrument setup.” At 5,063 per million, a well reading 1,000,000 puts about 5,000 into its neighbor. Promega sells the GloMax, so lean on the H1-against-itself pair.

Synergy Neo2

“< 0.1% in 96-well plate; < 0.25% in low-volume 384-well plate.” Nothing for 1536.

An AstraZeneca SLAS poster, as cited in a presentation, showed low-signal error bars “significantly higher on the Neo2.”

Tecan Spark

No crosstalk figure is published. Tecan says only that dedicated fibers for each plate format “minimizes crosstalk and gives luminometer-like performance”; the spec sheet and reference guide list no percentage.

Tecan’s MultiCheck Plus QC plate includes a luminescence crosstalk check for Spark, but the Tecan page lists no pass limit.

VANTAstar

Not published (spec page).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not published. Thermo’s own paper (D10893), Figure 5, plots luminescence crosstalk on a log scale outward from one bright well: still measurable several wells away, above 0.01% across much of the plate.

Fixed optics can’t focus into the well to cut it.

24 Luminescence light path: dedicated optics or a gap in the fluorescence optics

Luminescence light path: dedicated optics or a gap in the fluorescence optics
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Dedicated path by default (bypasses the LVF for maximum photons); can be routed through the LVF or a filter.

—
EnVision Nexus

Three paths: Standard and Enhanced on the two-PMT filter path; Ultra-sensitive on “a designated US detection unit” (option, one color, top only). Luminescence is never read on the fly: 1:13 per 384 plate against 0:13 for FI at the same 100 ms (5.6×, calculated).

—
PHERAstar FSX

Its own light path: sample, focus lens, optic module, matched PMT pair. No light source and no excitation side in the path. Top or bottom.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

“All Wavelengths” path, 300–650 nm, on the one cooled PMT shared with far-red fluorescence; bottom reads through a 675 nm short-pass filter.

—
Synergy H1

“Luminescence is measured through an empty filter position in the filter cube,” or a direct channel, “no filtering, white light only.” BioTek’s qualification reads it with the excitation position set to “Plug” and the emission to “Hole.”

—
Synergy Neo2

“Luminescence is measured through an empty filter position in the filter cube.” No luminescence optic of its own; even a luminescence-only lab needs a cube in the slot, and the single-detector top cube is “REQUIRED for top measurements.”

—
Tecan Spark

Dedicated luminescence PMT, photon counting. Every luminescence read is lid off, by Tecan’s own protocol: “select always without lid for luminescence!”

A university SOP: “ALWAYS choose NO when applying luminescence, as the detector is placed deep over the wells.”

VANTAstar

Separate top lens for luminescence, switched automatically; filters or LVF.

—
Varioskan LUX

Direct (no filter) or through a user-fitted filter, 360–670 nm, in the LAT module.

—

25 Multicolor luminescence and BRET: donor and acceptor read together or one after the other

Multicolor luminescence and BRET: donor and acceptor read together or one after the other
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Sequential, through the LVF monochromator at bandwidths to 100 nm, no filters needed; a new luciferase pair is a software setting. Promega dual-luciferase certified.

—
EnVision Nexus

Simultaneous on the filter path (dual-channel module) at Standard or Enhanced sensitivity only. The Ultra-sensitive mode reads one color, so BRET can’t use it; the sheet rates Ultra-sensitive “up to 25x” more sensitive than Enhanced.

A pharma BRET comparison: “certainly the Nexus was not better.”

PHERAstar FSX

Simultaneous, as standard, on two matched low-noise PMTs, top or bottom. NanoBRET 610/450 module in the catalog; any pair built to order.

Neither signal decays while waiting its turn.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Sequential on one PMT; sold as expansions. Two wavelengths lock the gain at High (documented for the i3x; not yet confirmed for the iD). Promega’s NanoBRET lists don’t name the iD3/iD5.

—
Synergy H1

Sequential: 485/20 then 640LP, 1 s each (BioTek’s own dual-luciferase note).

—
Synergy Neo2

Simultaneous top only, on two different kinds of detector; a comparison sheet: “the red-PMT performs poorly” for dual-emission BRET. No simultaneous BRET from the bottom. The two-color cube is “please contact BioTek.” Promega’s NanoBRET lists name no BioTek or Agilent reader.

—
Tecan Spark

Sequential, 300 ms each (Tecan’s NanoBRET note); “BRET ratios were computed manually.” Enhanced module only; software picks the filters. Promega’s NanoBRET instrument lists (2016, 2025) don’t name the Spark.

—
VANTAstar

Sequential, through filters or the LVF monochromators (no filters required).

—
Varioskan LUX

Sequential on one PMT; emission filters bought separately and fitted with a pick-up tool.

—

blocks.html:
26 Injection possible concurrent with detection?

Flash luminescence peaks as the reagent reaches the well and fades within seconds. A reader that injects elsewhere, or waits half a second, misses the peak. Only two readers here read while the reagent goes in.

Injection possible concurrent with detection?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Yes: injection at the read position. Up to two injectors, 3–500 µL, up to 420 µL/s; <30 µL dead volume; clear, user-replaceable tubing.

With the injection spoon fitted and lens protect off, the reader injects during measurement; no post-injection delay for true flash luminescence.

EnVision Nexus

Not published. The 77-page user manual has no injector or dispenser specification.

The 2008 EnVision’s sensitive detectors had no “real time” dispense-and-read mode, only a “shortened interval.”

PHERAstar FSX

Yes: injection at the read position, recording 50 readings per second through the injection. Two injectors, 3–500 µL, up to 420 µL/s, 0.5 mL prime. Any format to 1536.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No: luminescence reads wait “500 msec after injection ends” (800 ms for absorbance). Injectors not usable in FP or TRF; prime “at least 2 mL” plus 250 µL; plates must be unlidded; a PC is required for any injector protocol.

Peristaltic pumps: “The lifetime of the tubing is limited and you must replace the tubing when worn.” Accuracy ±(4% + 1 µL), so ≥14% at 10 µL (calculated).

Synergy H1

Injectors to 384 from an external dispense module; the manual says only that the tips go into “holes inside the reader” and gives no tip-to-optics position or dispense-to-read delay (the Neo2 manual gives one). Dead volume 1.1 mL; “minimum recommended prime volume is 2000 μL.”

Opaque tubing and tips out of sight; a poor fit for shared equipment.

Synergy Neo2

Injectors to 384 only, one well at a time, from an external module. Manual: the tips seat in holes inside the reader “behind the filter cube chamber(s)”; it specifies a maximum delay of < 1.0 second between end of dispense and start of read. Minimum prime 2,000 µL.

The manual never says the plate moves between dispense and read, or that the reader reads during injection; it gives only the tip location and the delay figure (p. 151, 96/384-well, default probe heights).

Tecan Spark

No. Injection position is away from the optics; the plate travels between inject and read. External module, opaque tubing, dead volume ≤100 µL.

The first light of a flash reaction happens where nothing is looking.

VANTAstar

No. Injection happens away from the read position: the reagent is added, then the well is read. Back-flush, heater and stirrer.

—
Varioskan LUX

Only with the dispensing head placed in the L position by hand. In the wrong position: “an extra plate movement… This may cause minor time delays between dispensing and measurement.” No dispensing with lidded-plate adapters or in 1536. Dead volume <100 µL.

—

blocks.html:
27 Time-resolved fluorescence sensitivity (europium)

Three readers have a laser; the other six excite TRF with a flash lamp. A laser delivers more UV light per flash, so fewer flashes per well are needed: the FSX reads a 1536-well HTRF plate in 36 s at Z′ 0.8 (Cisbio poster).

Time-resolved fluorescence sensitivity (europium)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<20 fM (384, 80 µL; <1.6 amol/well) with the Ultra HTRF/TRF module. Xenon flash lamp.

—
EnVision Nexus

Laser <4 fM (0.004 pM); lamp <20 fM (15 µL ProxiPlate). Laser is an option: diode-pumped solid state, 343 nm, “< 200 µJ” per pulse.

Field experience: a diode source, and not that powerful. A pharma site’s 2023 demo never tested the laser: “our unit laser was broken.”

PHERAstar FSX

Laser TRF: <5 fM (384, 80 µL; 0.4 amol/well), on a dedicated red-shifted PMT pair. HTRF Delta F >1100%.

Best TRF figure published on any reader in this matrix (tied with the Neo2 laser’s 5 fM, which is a typical in a different plate).

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD5 only. Standard 150 fM guaranteed; with the Enhanced TRF module 100 fM guaranteed, 10 fM optimized. iD3: not offered.

The module is fitted by the customer with a 2.0 mm hex key, instrument powered on. TRF module must be removed if some non TRF-modes are read. Not appropriate for shared equipment

Synergy H1

Data sheet <40 fM (no plate). Manual guarantee ≤250 fM, 96-well, more than 6× worse (calculated). Flash lamp; no laser offered.

—
Synergy Neo2

5 fM with the TRF laser, 40 fM with the lamp (384 low-volume, typical). Manual lamp figure: “≤ 250 fM (100 fM typical).” Laser ships only on Dual Filter Top builds, 7 of 19 part numbers.

Single Filter Top readers never get the laser, and the manual still sells it as “upgrade later.”

Tecan Spark

Filters ≤4 amol (100 µL) = 40 fM standard; ≤0.5 amol (20 µL) = 25 fM enhanced. Monochromator ≤10 amol / ≤0.7 amol. Flash lamp only; no laser. Calculated.

—
VANTAstar

<30 fM (384, 80 µL; <2.4 amol/well). Flash lamp, filters.

—
Varioskan LUX

<1 amol per well (white low-volume 384; volume not stated) = 50 fM at 20 µL (calculated). Fixed 334 nm excitation filter; flash lamp.

Calibration expires every 10 minutes.

28 HTRF certification, plate color, and how the two colors are read

Black plates cut crosstalk but return less light. Tecan gives the reason its monochromator path is not certified in black plates: “the light levels are too low.”

HTRF certification, plate color, and how the two colors are read
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Certified in black and white plates. Delta F >880% on the Cisbio control kit. Two colors read one after the other.

BMG’s brochure: “The ability to measure HTRF in black plates is only prerogative of the most sensitive readers.”

EnVision Nexus

HTRF certified; setup note: “This reader only allows high performance HTRF measurement when assays are run in WHITE plates.” Simultaneous on the filter path. Automatic HTRF ratio for lamp-plus-laser reads arrived as a new feature in January 2024.

A pharma HTS site “can’t export ratios as raw data” and could not obtain Revvity’s green 490/520 terbium module.

PHERAstar FSX

Certified in black and white plates; Delta F >1100%. Donor and acceptor at the same instant, from one laser flash, 60 flashes/s. A 1536 HTRF plate in 36 s at Z′ 0.8 (Cisbio poster).

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Certified for HTRF (iD5 + Enhanced TRF module). Sequential; two emissions lock the gain at High. MD’s own THUNDER note ranks the iD5 last of three MD readers on signal-to-background: iD5 3.4 · i3x 3.7 · M5e 4.5.

MD’s own Thunder TR-FRET application note ranks the iD5 last of three MD readers for TR-FRET.

Synergy H1

Cisbio-certified (BioTek’s June 2019 release lists the Synergy H1 among its “HTRF-certified detection systems”). Revvity’s H1 setup sheet allows filter-based mode only (“The monochromator mode is not HTRF compatible”) and says high-performance HTRF needs white plates. Two sequential reads (620 nm, then 665 nm) on one PMT; fixed 16 nm monochromator on most builds.

Certification: BioTek press release (26 Jun 2019): “BioTek’s other current HTRF-certified detection systems include the Synergy H1 Hybrid Multi-Mode Reader.” Setup sheet: Revvity, spc-htrf-setup-biotek-synergy-h1 (2024). The H1 data sheet does not mention HTRF.

Synergy Neo2

Certified white plates only. Simultaneous only on Dual Filter Top builds with a special-order cube; the 665 and 620 nm signals land on two different kinds of tube. A side-by-side test: Z′ “dropped significantly” when read fast (field test; data not held).

—
Tecan Spark

Sequential, one detector. Tecan: the monochromator path is “not certified for HTRF measurements in black plates, as the light levels are too low.” Every monochromator-emission configuration fails Cisbio’s ΔF criterion (419–420 against 600) because of the 20 nm band. 384 plate: 2:06 on filters, 10:37–13:50 on the monochromator.

—
VANTAstar

HTRF/TR-FRET through filters; Reader Control Kit Delta F >700%, figures published for black and white plates. Sequential.

—
Varioskan LUX

TR-FRET and HTRF listed; Thermo calls it a “Certified HTRF compatible reader by CisBio Bioassays” and names no plate colors. Sequential through one PMT; fixed 334 nm excitation.

The certification is Thermo's claim, not independently confirmed against Revvity's certified-reader list; the page's only plate statement is a TRF sensitivity quoted on a white low-volume 384-well plate.

30 Fluorescence polarization precision, top (SD at 1 nM fluorescein; smaller is better)

Four vendors moved four different conditions on the same spec: Agilent moved the plate format, MD moved the concentration, Tecan dropped the plate, Revvity dropped both. Ask for mP at 1 nM in the plate you use.

Fluorescence polarization precision, top (SD at 1 nM fluorescein; smaller is better)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

<0.5 mP (384sv, 20 µL). Instant polarizer switching.

Best FP figure published on any reader in this matrix (tied with the FSX).

EnVision Nexus

<1.15 mP (module 2001, fluorescein, 50 µL; plate and concentration not stated). Top read only. A 2024 “Detection Spot Size” option “can improve the data quality of bright FP applications” by collecting light from less of the well.

—
PHERAstar FSX

<0.5 mP (384sv black, 20 µL). Both planes read at once on the matched PMT pair, from the same flash, so lamp flicker cancels in the ratio.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD5 only. Filters: 5 mP guaranteed at 1 nM (1 mP optimized). Monochromator: 5 mP at 10 nM, ten times the dye. iD3: not offered.

The live spec page has dropped the monochromator figure.

Synergy H1

Data sheet 2 mP, no plate. Manual guarantees 5 mP, 96-well, with 60 measurements per data point. History: 5 mP (2010, 384), 5 mP (2016, 2022), 2 mP (2026). Same optical system.

Filters only, one assay per cube; no monochromator FP.

Synergy Neo2

Data sheet 1 mP, the only spec with no plate format. Manual: “< 5 mP standard deviation at 1 nM Sodium Fluorescein (1 mP typical)”; the installation test passes at <5. Dual-plane cube is special order.

The headline is the typical; a unit can ship at five times it.

Tecan Spark

Filters ≤1.5 / monochromator ≤3.0 mP (standard); ≤1.25 / ≤2.5 (enhanced). No plate, no volume. No FP on the Spark Cyto 300 and 400.

Through the monochromator FP precision is twice as poor, in Tecan’s own table.

VANTAstar

<1.2 mP (384sv, 20 µL), filters, top or bottom.

—
Varioskan LUX

Not offered, and by user reports can never be added.

—

Fluorescence polarization from the bottom
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

FP from the bottom: not stated for the Plus. BMG lists “Top and bottom reading” as a measurement mode and gives bottom sensitivity only for fluorescence intensity; its FP figure (< 0.5 mP SD at 1 nM FITC, 384sv, 20 µL) carries no top/bottom label.

Not offered. FP is top read only.

—

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not published.

—

Not possible. FP is filters-only and filters read top only.

—

One bottom detector, so the two planes are read one after the other, and the manual gives bottom FP no specification.

—
Tecan Spark

Not available. Tecan’s guide: “The polarization option is available for top measurements only.”

The 2015 spec sheet’s FP hardware table reuses a generic wavelength-range header that mentions top and bottom, but gives FP results with no top/bottom split; the 2024 guide is explicit.

VANTAstar

Yes, through filters, top or bottom.

—
Varioskan LUX

Not offered (no FP).

32 UV fluorescence polarization capable?

UV fluorescence polarization capable?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Yes: FP-UV option to 240 nm.

—
EnVision Nexus

No UV FP module listed. Revvity's four FP filter modules excite at 485, 535, 555 and 620 nm.

Kaleido lets a filter module be Custom type, so the catalogue does not strictly rule out a special-order UV FP module.

PHERAstar FSX

Polarization modules are built to order at any wavelength (three-filter polarization module). BMG's store lists a Pyrene FP module at 320 nm excitation (380 nm emission), and the spec table gives the FI/FP filter range as 230–750 nm. UV mP figure: not published.

The module's own description: “fluorophores with Exmax between 315 and 340 nm, such as pyrene”. The lowest FP module found in the PHERAstar FSX store list is this 320 nm one; the DPH module is 360 nm. BMG's FP page notes UV FP needs “specific UV polarizers”.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD5 with the optional UVIS polarizer, to 300 nm.

—
Synergy H1

Partly. The stock excitation polarizer is “visible-range (400 nm and above, the default)”; a UV polarizer (300 nm and above) is a separate BioTek option. The manual’s FP spec lists excitation 330–700 nm (UV-transparent polarizing filter); the current data sheet prints 280–700 nm.

Manual and data sheet disagree on the short-wavelength limit (330 vs 280 nm); the manual’s UV polarizer is rated 300 nm and above.

Synergy Neo2

Yes on paper: Agilent’s data sheet gives the FP wavelength range as 280 to 700 nm (850 nm option), filter-based. The 2016 manual states no FP wavelength range; it says only that the filter cube must contain polarizing filters.

The sibling H1 manual says its UV excitation polarizer starts at 300 nm and its FP spec is 330-700 nm, yet the H1 data sheet also prints 280 nm; ask which polarizer part number delivers 280 nm.

Tecan Spark

Standard FP module starts at 390 nm; enhanced at 300 nm.

A 2023 quote carried FP from 390 nm while the customer held the enhanced spec sheet.

VANTAstar

Spec sheet lists FP among the filter modes covering 240–740 nm. BMG names no UV-FP option and publishes no UV mP figure for the VANTAstar.

On BMG's store, the CLARIOstar UV filter sets carry the footnote “For use in Fluorescence polarization your reader must be equipped with the UV FP option”; no equivalent VANTAstar option was found, and BMG's FP page says UV FP needs “specific UV polarizers”. Ask BMG applications whether the VANTAstar's 240 nm FP range includes UV polarizers.

Varioskan LUX

Not offered (no FP).

—

33 AlphaScreen / AlphaLISA specification and excitation source

Alpha signal moves about 8% per °C (PerkinElmer’s figure) and the beads bleach, so excitation source, temperature and what moves between wells all affect the result. Three readers here have no Alpha at all.

AlphaScreen / AlphaLISA specification and excitation source
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

680 nm laser module: <5 pM / <100 amol P-Tyr-100 (384sv, 20 µL). Can be added later.

—
EnVision Nexus

Two modes that cannot be combined: Enhanced (700 mW laser, 4:31 per 384, 79 pg/mL) and High-throughput (400 mW, 1:36, single channel, 121 pg/mL). HT mode: “wells outside the selected measurement layout are also exposed” (fixed 9 mm laser-to-PMT distance, two wells at 384 pitch).

Revvity’s own note says apertures exist to prevent “bleaching of neighboring Alpha samples”; in HT mode the laser reaches wells it hasn’t read yet. Room must be 20–25 °C. Alpha “cannot be added to a Loop operation.”

PHERAstar FSX

Dedicated 680 nm laser: <5 pM / <100 amol P-Tyr-100 (384sv white, 20 µL). Optic module set once per plate; nothing moves between wells.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not offered. MD’s Alpha lives on a different platform.

—
Synergy H1

Not offered. BioTek’s 2010 table marks AlphaScreen “n/a” for the H1, its “Value” hybrid.

—
Synergy Neo2

Laser Alpha (100 mW, 680 nm). Sensitivity: 100 amol LCK peptide (384-well low-volume plate). Alpha moves a cube twice per well: 768 moves per 384 plate. Not appropriate for high volume alpha use. Maintenance friction point.

The 2016 manual’s Alpha spec is only laser power (100 mW ± 10%); its Alpha acceptance test is crosstalk < 0.1% and SNR > 10 with Omnibeads, not a sensitivity pass line.

Tecan Spark

680 nm, 750 mW laser. Printed < 2.5 ng/mL Omnibeads; Tecan’s own brochure chart: 3.62 ng/mL uncorrected, 1.58 corrected. 384 wells in ≤2 min “incl. temp. corr.” On the Spark Cyto, Alpha only on the top model.

Without the software temperature correction, the Spark misses its own number.

VANTAstar

Not offered. No Alpha mode, no laser.

—
Varioskan LUX

LED excitation at 680 nm; no laser. Spec <100 amol. Calibration expires every 10 minutes; no cooling.

—

Alpha temperature handling: can the plate be held cool while it is read?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Lowest incubation setting ambient +3 °C. No cooling.

—

No cooling; floor ambient +5 °C. Alpha puts a specification on the room: “+20 °C to +25 °C, relative humidity < 80 %.”

A lab that drifts outside 20–25 °C overnight is outside Revvity’s Alpha conditions (inferred).

PHERAstar FSX

Advanced Assay Stability option holds the chamber at 18–45 °C, at or below room temperature, with cooled air over the detectors, electronics and chamber. CellTiter-Glo CV 1.8% with AAS against 3.2% without (BMG data). No external vents.

Lowest measurement-chamber temperature published on any reader in this matrix (tied with the Spark’s Te-Cool floor, which is a liquid loop with a condensation problem).

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not applicable (no Alpha).

—
Synergy H1

Not applicable (no Alpha).

—
Synergy Neo2

Alpha mode “3°C over ambient to 30°C,” room must be “less than 30°C.” No cooling.

In a 25 °C lab the Alpha window is 28–30 °C; at 27 °C there is no window at all (calculated).

Tecan Spark

Tecan corrects Alpha data for heat in software: “automatic normalization of the signal to a temperature of 22.5 °C,” every read time “incl. temp. corr.” Tecan says its electronics warm the chamber up to +4 °C. The hardware fix is Te-Cool (option), 18–42 °C.

At +4 °C that is about a third of the signal (calculated), corrected by a model, so every corrected well carries the model’s error. Te-Cool’s 18 °C floor is the dew point of a 30 °C lab at 50% humidity: condensation. Without its software temperature correction, Alpha misses Tecan’s own spec.

VANTAstar

Not applicable (no Alpha). Floor ambient +4 °C.

—
Varioskan LUX

No cooling; floor ambient +4 °C. When the 10-minute calibration can’t run, the Alpha read carries a warning that accuracy “may have suffered.”

43 Plate adapters, lids and plate-type restrictions

Plate adapters, lids and plate-type restrictions
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

None. Any plate geometry is defined in software.

—
EnVision Nexus

Lids and high-skirt plates are refused by the stacker, Enhanced and Ultra-sensitive luminescence and both Alpha modes. One plate type per stacker protocol; max filled plate 190 g.

—
PHERAstar FSX

None. Plate geometry user-definable.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Max plate height 22 mm with lid; SpectraCuvette adapters without a sticker “cannot be used.” Injected reads must be unlidded.

—
Synergy H1

Standard 6- to 384-well plates in the 128 x 86 mm footprint, plus Take3 and Take3 Trio; maximum plate height 0.8 in. (20.30 mm) for absorbance and 0.89 in. (22.6 mm) for fluorescence and luminescence. Optional PCR-tube and BioCell adapter plates. To read with a lid, create a Gen5 plate type that adds the lid height. For evaporation the manual says “Use microplate lids.”

Gen5 2.01 and later has a separate “Plate Lid adds” parameter (manual error-code table); other labware “can result in positioning errors during program execution.”

Synergy Neo2

Standard 6- to 1536-well plates in the 128 x 86 mm footprint, plus Take3 and Take3 Trio; maximum plate height 0.89 in. Optional PCR-tube and BioCell adapter plates. For lids the manual says to “create a new plate type in Gen5 with the correct Plate Height”; other labware “can result in positioning errors during program execution.” Injectors take only 6- to 384-well plates, and tip priming is not for tall plates.

Gen5’s protocol dialog also has a “Use lid” check box (manual p. 50).

Tecan Spark

ANSI/SBS plates, 10 mm (no lid) up to 24.5 mm (with lid) tall; for bottom reads the well bottom may sit no more than 5.5 mm above the plate rim. Lid Lifter pad needs a lid no taller than 11.5 mm; the Spark-Stack takes no lids. Luminescence is read lid off by Tecan’s protocol, and the humidity spec excludes the outside wells and is tested with a lid.

Tecan’s knowledge portal says of luminescence: “Don’t use transparent plates or plates with lids as this results in crosstalk between wells.” Cuvette adapter, NanoQuant Plate, MultiCheck plate and Cell Chip adapter “can be used with limitations for selected measurement techniques.”

VANTAstar

None listed.

—
Varioskan LUX

Every plate change is a hardware change: ten adapters by well count and lid; “Always use a plate adapter with a universal tray”; only five support dispensing and none of the lidded ones. The robotic adapter is held by washers and four retaining screws.

44 Fastest read of a 384-well dual-emission assay (two colors, whole plate)

The fair comparison is time for both colors at a stated flash count. A sequential reader needs a second emission read at every well; doubling its single-color time is the simple upper estimate (plate movement is shared, so the true figure can be somewhat less), and no vendor prints a dual-emission time, so the doubling is marked as an estimate.

Fastest read of a 384-well dual-emission assay (two colors, whole plate)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

One color in flying mode, 1 flash: 15 s; two colors are read one after the other, so about 30 s (estimated; BMG prints no dual-emission time). 10 flashes: 57 s per color.

—
EnVision Nexus

14 s on the fly (FI, FP, TRF) with a dual-channel module, both colors at once. Luminescence never on the fly: 1:13 per 384 plate.

—
PHERAstar FSX

14 s (flying mode, 1 flash) for both colors, because they are read at the same instant from the same flash. 10 flashes: 38 s. TRF laser, 1536 wells: 36 s.

The only reader here whose dual-emission time equals its single-color time.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

One color: ~32 s “using lowest setting and speed read”; two colors about 64 s (estimated), with the gain locked at High (documented for the i3x only). FP: 3 min per 384.

—
Synergy H1

One color: 22 s (kinetic figure, unchanged since 2010; no mode or flash count stated); two colors about 44 s (estimated).

—
Synergy Neo2

One color: 11 s (sweep mode). Simultaneous two-color read exists on Dual Filter Top builds with a special-order cube; no dual-emission time published. Sensitivity is qualified at Normal speed, 50 measurements per point.

The 11 s and the sensitivity spec come from different settings.

Tecan Spark

One color: 22–30 s, “one flash only,” plate in and out not included; two colors about 45–60 s (estimated). NanoBRET at Tecan’s 300 ms per channel: about 3 min 50 s for 384 (estimated). Extended range doubles it: “two consecutive measurement runs.”

—
VANTAstar

One color, flying, 1 flash: 16 s; two colors about 32 s (estimated).

—
Varioskan LUX

One color: 45 s minimum, one flash, carrier not stopping; two colors about 90 s (estimated), plus the 10-minute calibration clock on a long run.

blocks.html:
49 Heated measurement chamber, and whether the plate is read where it is heated

A temperature spec covers only the place it was measured. The Spark’s uniformity is specified at the incubation position, and the plate is read elsewhere.

Heated measurement chamber, and whether the plate is read where it is heated
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Yes, at the read position: ambient +3 °C to 45 °C, or 65 °C with the option. BMG’s measured plate gradient at 37 °C: 0.38 °C across an INHECO plate after three hours.

—
EnVision Nexus

Yes, heating only, ambient +5 to 65 °C; accuracy ±1 °C to 50, ±2 to 60, ±3 °C to 65. Uniformity across the plate: not published. “Oscillating temperatures in the lab will have an impact on temperature-sensitive assays.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

Yes: ambient +5 °C to 45 °C; with AAS, 18–45 °C independent of the room.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Yes, ambient +5 to 66 °C; from 55 °C up “ambient temperature of 25°C (77°F) is required.” The sensors read “the temperature of the air inside the chamber, not the temperature of the samples.” Equilibration about an hour.

—
Synergy H1

Yes, four-zone, ambient +4 to 45 °C (70 °C on the four M2 builds); ±0.5 °C at 37 °C.

—
Synergy Neo2

Yes, four-zone heating at the read position, ambient +4 to 65 °C. Alpha mode: ambient +3 to 30 °C.

—
Tecan Spark

Temperature is specified where the plate waits; the read happens somewhere else. Ambient +4 to 42 °C; uniformity <0.5 °C “at incubation position.” “The plate must be placed in incubation position while shaking or waiting.” On the Spark Cyto the chamber isn’t heated at all, only the parking spot.

A 384-well glow kinetic every 5 minutes spends about 55% of the run out of the incubation position, lid off (calculated from Tecan’s read time). Tecan says the chamber runs up to +4 °C over the room. Temperature is specified where the plate waits, and the plate is read somewhere else. “The plate must be placed in incubation position while shaking or waiting.”

VANTAstar

Yes, at the read position: ambient +4 °C to 45 °C, or 60 °C option. The optical head is heated too; the upper plate runs 0.5 °C above the lower to keep condensation off the lid.

—
Varioskan LUX

Yes, ambient +4 to 45 °C. The temperature holds “for as long as the software is connected to the instrument.”

A PC that sleeps or restarts mid-run takes the temperature control with it (inferred).

blocks.html:
50 Can the measurement chamber be held at or below room temperature (no forced +3–5 °C)?

Every reader warms its chamber with its own electronics. Assays that move with temperature (Alpha, glow luminescence, enzyme kinetics) are run at a temperature the reader chose unless it can cool. Two readers here can; one of them does it with a liquid loop and a condensation problem.

Can the measurement chamber be held at or below room temperature (no forced +3–5 °C)?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No. Floor is ambient +3 °C.

—
EnVision Nexus

No, in any generation. “The instrument cannot reach temperatures lower than the ambient temperature.” The printed “15–65 °C” means ambient +5 °C; in a 25 °C lab the floor is 30 °C (calculated). In a Temperature operation “Maintain Ambient Temperature… is not available.” “Fast Cooling” opens the plate door and runs a fan.

Air filters “are not accessible for the user… This may affect… the precision of the temperature control.”

PHERAstar FSX

Yes, with Advanced Assay Stability: 18–45 °C, at a setpoint independent of the room, including at or below ambient. Rotary-compressor cooling in a rear unit; no external vents; condensate evaporated outside the instrument. Adds ~10 cm of depth; 62 kg total; the stacker still fits.

Best uniformity is at ambient +3.5–4 °C rather than at the coldest setting (BMG data).

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No. Floor ambient +5 °C. The only cooling MD names is the detector’s.

—
Synergy H1

No. Floor ambient +4 °C.

—
Synergy Neo2

No. Floor ambient +4 °C (ambient +3 in Alpha mode).

—
Tecan Spark

Te-Cool option, 18–42 °C, a liquid cooler for the incubation position. With it fitted the room limit drops from 35 °C to 30 °C; at 30 °C and 50% humidity the 18 °C floor is the dew point (calculated). 512 mm tall; “Only Tecan authorized service technicians are allowed to prepare instrument for transportation.”

A university facility switches on an external chiller for anything below 28 °C. Cooling is at the incubation position; the plate is read elsewhere. The chamber runs warm, and Tecan measured what that does without TE-Cool. Glow signal +34% in six minutes at 4 °C over ambient; CV 7.7% against 0.3%.

VANTAstar

No. Floor ambient +4 °C.

—
Varioskan LUX

No. Floor ambient +4 °C.

—

52 Humidity-controlled incubation chamber?

The Spark is the only reader here with humidity control. It works at the incubation position, and Tecan’s protocol reads luminescence with the lid off.

Humidity-controlled incubation chamber?
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No. Evaporation is managed with sealers and gas-permeable membranes; BMG publishes guidance on which to use.

—
EnVision Nexus

No, and lids are barred with the stacker, in Enhanced and Ultra-sensitive luminescence, and in both Alpha modes.

—
PHERAstar FSX

No. AAS lowers evaporation by holding the chamber at or below room temperature; BMG publishes rates with and without it.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

No. The guide recommends a lid or seal, but “For reads with injection, plates must be unlidded.”

—
Synergy H1

No. “Use microplate lids.”

—
Synergy Neo2

No.

—
Tecan Spark

Yes: humidity cassette plus Lid Lifter. <10% evaporation over 4 days, “excluding outside wells… with lid” (60 of 96 wells, lid on; calculated). Luminescence is read lid off.

The humidity setup suits long assays but not vigorous shaking; it lives at the incubation position. Field experience: the quote often doesn’t make clear which incubation setup is in it.

VANTAstar

No. The upper heating plate runs 0.5 °C above the lower to keep condensation off lids and seals.

—
Varioskan LUX

No. A lidded plate takes a different adapter, and no lidded adapter supports dispensing.

—

55 Number of included software licenses

On the iD, the touchscreen leads to SoftMax Pro seats and a separate Import license.

Number of included software licenses
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Unlimited. Control and MARS analysis software install on any number of PCs; multi-user control software for shared labs.

—
EnVision Nexus

One Revvity-supplied PC, bound to one serial number (“you cannot exchange the PCs between the devices”). Further analysis in MyAssays Desktop, a separate program, via XML export.

—
PHERAstar FSX

Unlimited. Reader control and MARS on any number of PCs.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

SoftMax Pro: one reader per license, four installs, three analysis-only seats, “per-seat product key activation.” Bringing touchscreen data into the software is extra: “Data import feature requires a separate license.” Updates “require a purchase” (i3x guide).

QuickSync puts SoftMax Pro on every user’s PC, and each departing student means another seat. Field experience: over a few years of lab turnover the seats can approach the cost of the reader. “Per-seat product key activation”; “Data import feature requires a separate license.”

Synergy H1

“A single Gen5 license includes 5 passwords for installation on 5 different computers.” Registration required.

Field notes (2016): Gen5 won’t merge data from separate runs.

Synergy Neo2

Five installations, each authorized by a USB dongle. Additional licenses are options.

Field note: “It isn’t clear what happens if the USB key is lost.”

Tecan Spark

Two installs of SparkControl. A new PC or Windows version has meant buying again (field notes).

Two Tecan software stacks that don’t talk: a university SOP says the Spark software “does not communicate with the Magellan software.”

VANTAstar

Unlimited. BMG: the software “can be installed on as many computers as needed.” No touchscreen available.

—
Varioskan LUX

“No limit on the number of licenses” and “no annual fee.” SkanIt 4.0 and 4.1 “cannot be installed in parallel on the same computer.”

—

56 Touchscreen or embedded computer, and what still needs a PC

No BMG reader has a touchscreen. The iD5’s touchscreen is a built-in computer that MD’s own support tells customers to bypass for anything beyond an endpoint, and it is the part that fails.

Touchscreen or embedded computer, and what still needs a PC
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No embedded computer. Runs from a PC.

—
EnVision Nexus

A Revvity-supplied desktop PC on a point-to-point cable that uses its network port; “The connection must not go through the customer’s network.” Windows 10 IoT LTSC 2021 only; domain join not guaranteed; virtual PCs not supported. Release notes: “Multi-tasking on the device PC during measurements can cause loss of data.”

Field notes: the local database stops at 90% (≈9 GB) and no new run starts until data is deleted or exported. A pharma site moves its data through a second PC to reach its network. The Quick Start Guide prints a default Windows login for the control PC.

PHERAstar FSX

No embedded computer. Runs from any PC.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Touchscreen on a built-in computer (“Data is stored on the reader’s hard drive”), NFC or PIN login, QuickSync to a networked PC. Walk-up ends at a single-wavelength endpoint: kinetic, multi-wavelength and spectrum data need a PC, a SoftMax Pro seat and the purchased Import feature; injectors, FRET, TR-FRET and Western blot are PC-only. Connect a PC and the touchscreen locks.

MD support: “I recommend performing the read through SoftMax Pro and not the touchscreen.” When the built-in computer fails, the interface fails and the repair is charged as an instrument repair. A university iD3 failed twice on the same part just past warranty. ResearchGate: “Has anyone had problems with the built-in computer of the Spectramax ID3?”

Synergy H1

No embedded computer. Gen5 on a PC.

—
Synergy Neo2

No embedded computer. Gen5 on a PC, a USB key per PC.

—
Tecan Spark

No embedded computer. Runs from a PC with SparkControl; the dashboard and Magellan don’t share methods.

—
VANTAstar

No embedded computer. Runs from a PC (SMART Control or Voyager).

—
Varioskan LUX

No computer or screen on the instrument. Every run goes through a PC running SkanIt: “To avoid data loss, make sure your computer does not go into hibernation/sleep during a measurement.”

—

59 Upgrade path: what can be added later, and what is fixed at purchase

Check the quote against the spec sheet here. Four of the six competitors print one sheet and sell many part numbers, so a figure on the sheet may come from a build or option the quote leaves out.

Upgrade path: what can be added later, and what is fixed at purchase
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Alpha, Ultra HTRF/TRF, LVis, stacker and barcode can be added later, one grade each. Bottom reading and luminescence are modules.

—
EnVision Nexus

Alpha is chosen at purchase: Enhanced or High-throughput, never both. HT Alpha “automatically also includes Luminescence (Ultra-sensitive)”; a rep in writing would not quote one without the other. Field retrofit of option modules: not published. New filter modules depend on Revvity making them.

The headline numbers belong to options: Ultra-sensitive luminescence, both Alpha modes, the TRF laser, the stacker and Part 11 are all line items.

PHERAstar FSX

Spectrometer, TRF, TRF laser, Alpha laser, injectors, AAS and stacker are options, and each “can also be added later.”

One instrument at one performance grade; a lab never trades up to a different model to gain a mode.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

iD3 → iD5 is a different reader. Upgrades: bottom luminescence (factory only), Enhanced TRF module (customer-fitted with a hex key), gas mixer (“user-installable”), UVIS polarizer, red filter slides, injectors, Import license, GxP edition.

The brochure describes an iD5 with options the base reader doesn’t have, so a quote needs checking line by line.

Synergy H1

“Upgrade options are available; contact BioTek Customer Care.” Cubes can be added any time. Whether a fixed 16 nm build can become variable bandwidth: not published. 12 part numbers; variable bandwidth and 70 °C only on the four M2 builds; injectors “sold separately” on every one.

—
Synergy Neo2

Single or Dual Filter Top is fixed at purchase; no part number has both. The TRF laser comes only with the dual top. 19 part numbers; six have no monochromator for fluorescence or luminescence; one (N2MON) has no filters.

The manual still sells the laser as “upgrade later.”

Tecan Spark

Modular, in standard and enhanced grades. On the Spark Cyto the ladder removes as it climbs: 400 gains a monochromator and loses filters, 500 the reverse, both only on the 600 with Alpha bundled.

The spec sheet describes the enhanced modules. The quote may not: a 2023 university quote carried standard absorbance, aperture, bottom reading and luminescence.

VANTAstar

Detection modes, injectors and extended temperature can be added later. The optics choice is fixed at purchase: the filter-only VANTAstar F can’t take LVF monochromators later.

—
Varioskan LUX

“Modular, upgradeable.” FP can never be added (user reports). A new LAT module arrives needing the user’s own calibration: “You must run the calibration.” Modes are letters in the catalog code (L, A, T, D, G); a missing letter is a missing mode.

—

60 Validation plates, qualification and service terms

Validation plates, qualification and service terms
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

Evaluation Plate is sold for IQ/OQ-type validation (NIST-traceable absorbance filters plus solid fluorescence and luminescence standards). BMG US service plans: Standard Depot includes a yearly QCPM; only Preferred Onsite includes a loaner. Repair turnaround: not published.

From BMG’s US store: Standard Depot “includes parts and labor coverage, free software and firmware updates, and a yearly quality control and preventative maintenance (QCPM)”; Preferred Onsite adds “loaner equipment in case your reader is out of service for an extended time.” Plan availability “may depend on product and country.”

EnVision Nexus

“Repair and service may only be performed by the Revvity Service.” Air filters “not accessible for the user… let Revvity Service check the filters once a year.” Remote support is LogMeIn Rescue; declining it “may increase costs for the service contract.” Lamp, laser and PMT service life: not published.

A two-Nexus pharma site’s service technician “had no idea how to service the instrument.”

PHERAstar FSX

Evaluation Plate is sold for IQ/OQ-type validation (NIST-traceable absorbance filters plus solid fluorescence and luminescence standards); the FSX page also lists optional QC internal standards. BMG US service plans: Standard Depot includes a yearly QCPM; only Preferred Onsite includes a loaner. Repair turnaround: not published.

Same US service plans as the CLARIOstar Plus. BMG’s US store also sells a Phosentix MicroQC Performance Testing Plate for the FSX.

SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

MD’s LM1 validation plate checks 2.5–3 decades of luminescence on multimode readers and skips the dim rungs as “too dim to measure,” so the 7-decade claim is never re-checked on the customer’s unit. Three SpectraTest plates, one per mode: “it must be returned to Molecular Devices. Only Molecular Devices has the necessary knowledge and equipment to recertify”; yearly; book a month ahead. Repair is at MD’s depot: “Instruments not covered by Warranty or Service Plan are not eligible for a loaner.”

MD “is not liable for damage incurred during shipment.”

Synergy H1

OQ yearly; PQ monthly or quarterly. The absorbance test plate is recertified annually by BioTek; FP and TRF tests need a dedicated qualification cube. Lamp “not user-changeable.”

—
Synergy Neo2

Terms: the manual recommends the OQ “initially (before first use)” and then annually, and absorbance test plates are recertified by BioTek annually; warranty terms ship as a separate document and no length is printed in the manual. The luminescence OQ is one point at one gain, so the “>6 decades” is never re-checked on the customer’s unit. Wear to plan for: 768 cube moves per 384-well Alpha plate, an injector module needing a daily flush and overnight soak, and two xenon lamps “(not user-changeable).” Daily flushing is a warranty matter: “Failure to follow preventive maintenance protocols may void the warranty.”

Agilent’s US Terms of Sale (Apr 2024) say only that “Each Product receives a global warranty which includes the standard warranty for the country of purchase” and refer to a separate warranty page; the instrument warranty length was not found.

Tecan Spark

Tecan lists “QC tools for IQOQ services”: the MultiCheck Plus QC plate, which Tecan recalibrates at its factory annually. The guide calls for an annual maintenance procedure by a Tecan service engineer. Te-Care contracts list a loaner only as a billed option (footnote: “Subject to availability”); the 48-hour onsite response is in COMPLETE only.

Te-Care and QC-plate terms are from Tecan’s web pages (tecan.com/service-contracts, Detection & Others tab; lifesciences.tecan.com/microplate-readers-qc-tools); regional differences apply.

VANTAstar

Evaluation Plate sold as an accessory (NIST-traceable absorbance filters plus solid fluorescence and luminescence standards). BMG US service plans: Standard Depot includes a yearly QCPM; only Preferred Onsite includes a loaner. Repair turnaround: not published.

Same US service plans as the CLARIOstar Plus.

Varioskan LUX

Verification plates: spectrophotometric (N03394) and Lumiwell luminescence (2806460), plus a “Microplate package for Varioskan LUX IQ/OQ” (SP-00720). Warranty and service-plan terms for the LUX are not published. Thermo's Part 11 table puts validation and user training on the customer.

Thermo's generic Unity Lab Services plan page does not name the Varioskan or plate readers, and the Dana-Farber quote's “2Y WARR” is a customer quote, not a published term.

61 Support lifetime and end-of-service history

Support lifetime and end-of-service history
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

By BMG’s own account, no BMG reader has ever been phased out of service support.

—
EnVision Nexus

One Windows build for the life of the PC: Windows 10 IoT LTSC 2021, “No, the license is only valid exactly for” that version, supported to January 2032. Kaleido upgrades run one way (4.0 data into 4.1, “but not vice versa”). Revvity publishes no instrument end-of-support policy for the Nexus.

Revvity's service terms reserve the right to refuse a repair order for instrument obsolescence or parts availability, but set no minimum support period.

PHERAstar FSX

“Any 16-bit unit will have a guaranteed 10 years of support from the point of purchase.” No BMG reader phased out of support.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Not published. MD’s repair FAQ states no obsolescence policy.

—
Synergy H1

No end-of-service date found for the H1 (on sale since 2010). Sibling Synergy Mx: discontinued 2015, service ended Oct 1, 2022 (BioTek’s 2021 notice). H4, Synergy 2 and HT no longer sold or supported.

—
Synergy Neo2

Agilent’s published Service Terms let it drop a product from service coverage on 60 days’ written notice; no Neo2-specific support-life period is published. Support for the sibling Synergy Mx ended ~5.5 years after one account’s purchase. Labs are replacing BioTek readers that BioTek stopped supporting (field experience).

The clause governs service agreements and sets a notice period, not a minimum support life; the Neo2 manual, data sheet and product page state no support-life commitment.

Tecan Spark

Tecan’s own schedule: Infinite M1000 shipped to March 2012, support ended March 2019: “no sales, no service packs, no modifications (we expect customers to upgrade in case of problems).” About seven years from sale. The Spark is based on the M1000 (user reports).

Tecan has since removed the schedule from its website; an archived copy exists.

VANTAstar

“Free tech and application support for the lifetime of the reader” (BMG value sheet).

—
Varioskan LUX

Not published. Thermo gives no support-lifetime or end-of-service policy for the LUX. The Varioskan Flash page is marked discontinued and points to the LUX, with no end-of-service date.

—

62 Relocation: what moving the reader down the hall involves

Relocation: what moving the reader down the hall involves
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

No restriction. 32 kg, two people.

—
EnVision Nexus

“Allow the instrument to acclimatize for at least 24 hours after shipping or transport.” Stacker removal “may only be carried out by a Revvity service engineer.” 90 kg; 100 kg with stacker. “Sensitive to vibrations.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

Nothing extra to disconnect; AAS has no external vents or plumbing.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

Moving terms: a customer procedure (guide p. 125) that does not call for a Molecular Devices engineer: remove filter slides and any Enhanced TRF module, touch “Lock Instrument,” fit the transport locks, lift with at least two people. “The instrument can be damaged if the transport locks are not removed before the instrument is powered on.” 40 kg. Original packaging is called for only to store, ship or move it to another building, and warranty claims are void if transport damage is caused by improper packing.

The iD3 guide carries the same procedure (p. 98); the iD5e guide renames the touchscreen step “Prepare Shipment - Lock Instrument.”

Synergy H1

Shipping brackets must go back in, in original packaging “designed to be used no more than five times.” Shipping any other way “can void the warranty.”

—
Synergy Neo2

No restriction found in the manual.

—
Tecan Spark

“Do not ship an instrument with integrated cooling module! Only Tecan authorized service technicians are allowed to prepare instrument for transportation. Residual cooling fluid might damage the instrument.”

Moving a Te-Cool Spark starts with a service call; a field note: versions you can’t move yourself without voiding the warranty.

VANTAstar

No restriction found. 27 kg.

—
Varioskan LUX

Refit the tray-holder transport lock before moving it (front cover off, four screws, ten steps), keep the original packaging, and plan a two-person lift at 53-60 kg. Thermo also offers a service to move the instrument.

The manuals give 53-60 kg (the product page lists 57 kg), not 54-59 kg, and do not say whether the per-unit luminescence alignment must be repeated after a move.

64 Field accounts and public reviews (reported, not independently established)

Reported accounts, not independent tests. Use these accounts to identify questions for further investigation.

Field accounts and public reviews (reported, not independently established)
ReaderSpecification or findingNotes and conditions
CLARIOstar Plus

SelectScience: five stars, two years after launch (2021).

—
EnVision Nexus

A pharma HTS site with two Nexus readers “no one is using”: modules unobtainable, PC off the domain, exports breaking LIMS. A biotech called its demo “a disaster” (broke twice, missing accessories). 2023 pharma demo: “our unit laser was broken.” A pharma BRET comparison: “certainly the Nexus was not better.”

—
PHERAstar FSX

1536 LanthaScreen (2013): matched a competing HTS reader’s 15-minute assay quality in 6 minutes, with a 40% larger window. Customers at a 2023 show said a competitor’s new flagship looked like a copy of it.

—
SpectraMax iD3 / iD5

SelectScience iD3 page (April 2025): 3.2 / 5 from six reviews, featured quote “Don’t buy this one.” A university iD3’s built-in computer failed twice on the same part just past warranty; MD would not cover it; the group bought another make. r/labrats: two MD units returned for refund in ten years.

MD’s tagline on the same page: “Unparalleled performance on a personalized platform.”

Synergy H1

A core facility’s handwritten sign: “Please measure nano orange and mCherry plates with filter cubes, not with the monochromator!” In 2026 an Agilent rep sent a customer an AI-drafted comparison labeled a “3rd party Competitive review.”

That comparison gives the H1MF “~7 logs” and concedes the competing BMG reader “up to ~8 logs.”

Synergy Neo2

Almost no high-volume Alpha labs (field experience ties it to the 768-move design). NanoBRET, 2018: “Can’t do it from the bottom.” Caution: in a 2013 top-read TR-FRET demo the original Neo held its own.

—
Tecan Spark

A San Diego biotech’s new Spark couldn’t read its assays; service couldn’t fix it; the replacement failed the same way; they switched makes, and the director will take calls. A 2024 European demo: “The Spark… was slow and had bad performance for this plate.”

—
VANTAstar

SelectScience: 4.8 of 5, five reviews, 2023–2025.

—
Varioskan LUX

A genomics lab’s own PicoGreen QC test at matched 45 µL: signal over background 14.5, 5.2 and 15.2 against 32.9, 29.7 and 31.8 on the reader the lab bought; the lab put the Varioskan above its 20% CV limit. Slide: “Varioskan does not like Picogreen at low conc.”

A 2022 competitive view: “They haven’t released a new reader in years.”

tables.caption: Fluorescence sensitivity, top, filters (fluorescein, converted to pM where the vendor gives a volume)
rows: <2 pM (module 1001, 485/535 nm; 50 µL, 384 OptiPlate) = 100 amol; a comparison sheet gives 200 amol. Flash count not stated.
Excitation exists at 340, 355, 400, 485, 535, 555 and 632 nm only. A dye in between has no module. The filter-module list is sparse.
Free-air light path: lenses, no fiber bundles.
iD5 only: 3 pM guaranteed, 0.5 pM optimized (384; volume not stated). iD3: no filters.
The iD3 has no filter path at all; every iD3 fluorescence read is a monochromator read.
0.25 pM / 25 amol (384, works out to 100 µL). Manual guarantee: ≤10 pM (96-well; 3 pM typical in the IFU).
Filters read from the top only. The sheet figure is 40× better than the guarantee.

0.2 pM / 4 amol (384 low-volume, 20 µL), typical. 1536: 1 pM (10 µL). BioTek’s brochure calls these “the average observed factory test values”; the 2016 manual (Appendix A) guarantees <5 pM filters and ≤20 pM monochromator, 25× and 10× the averages.
Sensitivity is qualified at Normal speed with 50 measurements per point; the 11 s sweep-mode speed on the same sheet comes from a different setting.
Standard: ≤25 amol in 100 µL = 0.25 pM. Enhanced: ≤8 amol in 10 µL (1536) = 0.8 pM. Calculated.
Quoted at fluorescein, the one color the standard module’s single 510 nm dichroic sits at. The manual’s binding spec for the standard module is <10 pM (40× the brochure).
Not offered. Fluorescence intensity is monochromator only; the Varioskan’s filters serve luminescence, Alpha, BRET and TRF.
There is no filter path to fall back on when a fluorescence assay needs more light.

No gain to set on the Ultra-sensitive photon counter and no published count-rate ceiling. Filter-path PMTs: no gain setting in any Kaleido 4.1 operation; the only bright-sample control it names is an “Attenuated” filter-module property.

8 decades in one visit to the well (EDR). 700,000,000 counts.
Works in kinetics and with a stacker. Flying mode, the fastest read, runs at a fixed gain without EDR; in standard mode EDR’s test flash fits inside the pause the read already takes.

Kinetics run at a fixed gain chosen before the run, “a nominal dynamic range of three decades” per gain (MD, 2026). Endpoints get AutoPMT: a pre-read at High, then re-reads of saturated wells at Medium and Low.

MD’s own Figure 3: High saturates at 33 nM, Medium at 333 nM, Low is “losing sensitivity at low concentration.” The iD5 widens range for endpoints by re-reading saturated wells and, in fluorescence, by adjusting lamp intensity; it can’t do that in a kinetic or in luminescence. “For kinetic read, the PMT settings have to be fixed”; each gain covers “a nominal dynamic range of three decades.”

A single read tops out at 99,999 RFU; the manual’s remedy for saturation is “Try lowering the gain/sensitivity” (read again). BioTek’s 2010 table gave 5 decades; the 2026 sheet says 7 for the same model.
Gain is set per read, by number or scaled to a well the user picks as brightest.

Fixed gain per read, ceiling 10 million counts. “Auto-ranging” runs a gain check on every well and adds minutes per plate. BioTek support: use manual gain “for kinetic tests, rapid reads or for tests that require high sensitivity.”
Extended range by re-reading is possible for endpoints; for flash luminescence BioTek’s own tips say it is “simply not possible.”

One gain, chosen before the read, about 3–4 decades usable (inferred from Tecan’s help text). Tecan’s “extended dynamic range” is “Two consecutive measurement runs with a high and a low amplification” with the listed drawback “Long measurement times.”

Every one of Tecan’s four gain modes has a printed “Disadvantages” panel. Optimal mode: “If signal intensities within one plate are very far spread, certain signals might not be detected any more.” Two passes means the same well is read twice, at two moments; a kinetic can’t hold its timing. The two-pass method does widen the effective range for endpoints. Extended range is “Two consecutive measurement runs”; its listed drawback: “Long measurement times.”
8 decades in a single measurement (EDR), gain set per well in <0.1 s.
Auto gain picks one of four calibrated gains per well from a trial flash. Product page commits to FI >6 decades; the tech note shows seven.
Whether auto gain runs in kinetic reads: not published. The gain is chosen before the signal moves.

One low-noise PMT; CCD spectrometer. Two colors read one after the other. No red-shifted option.

Grating monochromators. Blocking figure: not published. The error table, on a monochromator read: “the luminescence probe may be picking up stray light. Try installing a plug in the filter cube.”

Gratings and slits; light guides carry light to and from the well. Light is lost at four points (excitation slit, delivery optic, emission light guide, emission slit).

No BRET or two-color luminescence from the bottom.
Not confirmed. No bottom luminescence found in Tecan’s manual (field notes).

Luminescence from the bottom offered. Bottom figure: not published; BMG gives one LUM figure, < 0.8 pM (< 15 amol/well ATP, 384sv, 20 µL), with no top/bottom label, and lists bottom figures only for fluorescence intensity.
BMG's own wording that bottom luminescence is offered: “Full top/bottom detection capability with automatic switch” (product page features).

tables.caption: Practical luminescence dynamic range in one gain setting
rows: 8 decades in a single measurement (EDR), bright and dim wells on one plate without a second read.

Revvity: “>8 logs” (Ultra-sensitive). No dead time, correction or overflow limit published. Analysis of a pharma customer’s paired plates found counting losses consistent with a ~48 ns dead time (about 20% at 5.4 million counts/s, before any correction).

Ask Revvity what Kaleido does about dead time and what appears when the detector’s over-light line goes high. Revvity documents no warning when high standards start to compress; in the customer’s plates, Z′ improved as signal was lost. The loss figures are before any dead-time correction. Past saturation, a counter’s reading falls as light rises, and no correction can recover that.
8 decades in one visit to the well (EDR). 200,000,000 counts
>7 decades as an endpoint figure (AutoPMT per well). Kinetics: a fixed gain, “a nominal dynamic range of three decades.” Low gain “requires Attenuation/Optical Density setting 0–3.”
The lamp-intensity trick that widens fluorescence range does not exist in luminescence.

Not published in decades or counts. Gen5 marks overflow above 99,998 counts; in BioTek’s own luciferase note the operator set the gain by hand to stay “below the photomultiplier tube (PMT) saturation threshold (overflow).”
Agilent: “> 6 decades.” With flash assays, extended range is “simply not possible” (BioTek’s own tips).
The Neo2 can widen effective range for glow endpoints by re-reading at a second gain.
>9 decades with gray attenuation filters (OD1–OD3; standard module OD1, OD2) chosen before the read. The enhanced module’s extra decade is the OD3 filter (inferred).
The Spark reaches those decades by picking a dimming filter before the read; the plate is still read at one gain. The Spark can also widen effective range by reading the plate twice.
>7 decades. Every luminescence calibration adds a dark-level check “to compensate for possible electronic component and photomultiplier signal level drift”; calibration expires every 10 minutes.

Promega dual-luciferase certified through the LVF at 100 nm bandwidth.
No. No monochromator in any mode.
No monochromator. Luminescence through dedicated filter optics, matched PMT pair.
Yes, monochromator path to 850 nm; its sensitivity is not published. The live spec page prints “Lumi: 300–850 nm” with no qualifier.
The headline range comes from the path with no published sensitivity.
Yes, for spectral scans, at the fixed 16 nm band on most builds.
Yes, luminescence spectra on the monochromator, 230–999 nm. Sensitive luminescence runs through the cube’s empty filter position.
Enhanced module only: software picks from 38 internal filters; the user can’t. Standard module: single-color luminescence. Luminescence spectra on the enhanced module.
Center wavelength and bandwidth show up grayed out in SparkControl.
Yes. Filters (240–740 nm) or LVF monochromators (320–740 nm), spectra included.
Yes, spectral luminescence up to 384-well, through the fixed 12 nm emission slit.

tables.caption: Integrated crosstalk apertures (the mask between plate and detector that blocks neighboring wells)?
rows: Yes. BMG’s application note AN371: an aperture spoon “is set up directly on top of the target well.” Crosstalk figure: not published on bmglabtech.com.
AN371 (2022) gives mathematical crosstalk-correction factors (white 0.05353%, gray 0.01277%, black 0.00026%), not an aperture crosstalk figure.

Yes, but hand-swapped per plate format, in gloves, through a transfer plate and a wizard. 2023 manual: the match “is not validated by the software,” beside a legend reading “Does not produce reasonable data or even damages the instrument.” The 2024 warning can be dismissed: “You can ignore the warning and start the measurement in any case.”
A wrong aperture still produces a completed run. With an aperture in, the read height is fixed. Field notes: a mis-load can drop an aperture inside the instrument.
Yes: aperture spoons, one per plate format (96/384, 1536, 3456). The FSX manual offers them to “reduce crosstalk even further in certain applications.” Crosstalk figure: not published.
None described. Field reports: MD support “requests that customers use every other well when this is an issue,” which gives up half the plate.
None. No aperture is described anywhere in the H1 manual; luminescence reads through an empty cube position.

No aperture between the plate and the optics. The aperture sits inside the cube, after the collecting lens, where light from the neighbors has already been gathered (inferred). Crosstalk control is bought as “high sensitivity” and “low cross talk” cube variants.
Three BRET assays can mean six cubes. The “low cross talk” cube gives up much of the signal.
“Enhanced Aperture” is a separate line item. A 2023 university quote left it out.
Yes, automatic: built-in luminescence crosstalk reduction, applied automatically up to 384 wells, no parts to place. Figure: not published.

A “crosstalk shield” after the light is collected, from one detection position. Thermo’s remedies: a smaller aperture that works “by decreasing luminescense signals,” and re-aligning the LAT module after cleaning or service.

tables.caption: Published luminescence crosstalk figure
rows: Not published (brochure and spec page checked).

Revvity’s figures are on its own AlphaPlates: “Most white plates show light leakage… This cannot be prevented by the optical design of a plate reader.” On White OptiPlate, Ultra-sensitive crosstalk was 0.70%, the worst of the three modes.
Not published on bmglabtech.com or in the FSX specification table.
<0.1% in 96-well half-area, <0.2% in 384 small-volume, white Costar. Clear-bottom bottom reads: <0.4%.
Not published. Promega measured one H1 two ways, 96-well: 530 vs 5,063 RLU per 10⁶, depending on which mode the software was in first (9.6× apart).

Promega’s caption: “The same multimode reader produces differing well-to-well cross talk dependent upon instrument setup.” At 5,063 per million, a well reading 1,000,000 puts about 5,000 into its neighbor. Promega sells the GloMax, so lean on the H1-against-itself pair.
“< 0.1% in 96-well plate; < 0.25% in low-volume 384-well plate.” Nothing for 1536.
An AstraZeneca SLAS poster, as cited in a presentation, showed low-signal error bars “significantly higher on the Neo2.”

No crosstalk figure is published. Tecan says only that dedicated fibers for each plate format “minimizes crosstalk and gives luminometer-like performance”; the spec sheet and reference guide list no percentage.
Tecan’s MultiCheck Plus QC plate includes a luminescence crosstalk check for Spark, but the Tecan page lists no pass limit.

Not published. Thermo’s own paper (D10893), Figure 5, plots luminescence crosstalk on a log scale outward from one bright well: still measurable several wells away, above 0.01% across much of the plate.
Fixed optics can’t focus into the well to cut it.

tables.caption: Luminescence light path: dedicated optics or a gap in the fluorescence optics
rows: Dedicated path by default (bypasses the LVF for maximum photons); can be routed through the LVF or a filter.

Three paths: Standard and Enhanced on the two-PMT filter path; Ultra-sensitive on “a designated US detection unit” (option, one color, top only). Luminescence is never read on the fly: 1:13 per 384 plate against 0:13 for FI at the same 100 ms (5.6×, calculated).
Its own light path: sample, focus lens, optic module, matched PMT pair. No light source and no excitation side in the path. Top or bottom.
“All Wavelengths” path, 300–650 nm, on the one cooled PMT shared with far-red fluorescence; bottom reads through a 675 nm short-pass filter.

“Luminescence is measured through an empty filter position in the filter cube,” or a direct channel, “no filtering, white light only.” BioTek’s qualification reads it with the excitation position set to “Plug” and the emission to “Hole.”

“Luminescence is measured through an empty filter position in the filter cube.” No luminescence optic of its own; even a luminescence-only lab needs a cube in the slot, and the single-detector top cube is “REQUIRED for top measurements.”
Dedicated luminescence PMT, photon counting. Every luminescence read is lid off, by Tecan’s own protocol: “select always without lid for luminescence!”
A university SOP: “ALWAYS choose NO when applying luminescence, as the detector is placed deep over the wells.”
Separate top lens for luminescence, switched automatically; filters or LVF.
Direct (no filter) or through a user-fitted filter, 360–670 nm, in the LAT module.

tables.caption: Multicolor luminescence and BRET: donor and acceptor read together or one after the other
rows: Sequential, through the LVF monochromator at bandwidths to 100 nm, no filters needed; a new luciferase pair is a software setting. Promega dual-luciferase certified.

Simultaneous on the filter path (dual-channel module) at Standard or Enhanced sensitivity only. The Ultra-sensitive mode reads one color, so BRET can’t use it; the sheet rates Ultra-sensitive “up to 25x” more sensitive than Enhanced.
A pharma BRET comparison: “certainly the Nexus was not better.”
Simultaneous, as standard, on two matched low-noise PMTs, top or bottom. NanoBRET 610/450 module in the catalog; any pair built to order.
Neither signal decays while waiting its turn.
Sequential on one PMT; sold as expansions. Two wavelengths lock the gain at High (documented for the i3x; not yet confirmed for the iD). Promega’s NanoBRET lists don’t name the iD3/iD5.
Sequential: 485/20 then 640LP, 1 s each (BioTek’s own dual-luciferase note).

Simultaneous top only, on two different kinds of detector; a comparison sheet: “the red-PMT performs poorly” for dual-emission BRET. No simultaneous BRET from the bottom. The two-color cube is “please contact BioTek.” Promega’s NanoBRET lists name no BioTek or Agilent reader.

Sequential, 300 ms each (Tecan’s NanoBRET note); “BRET ratios were computed manually.” Enhanced module only; software picks the filters. Promega’s NanoBRET instrument lists (2016, 2025) don’t name the Spark.
Sequential, through filters or the LVF monochromators (no filters required).
Sequential on one PMT; emission filters bought separately and fitted with a pick-up tool.

tables.caption: Injection possible concurrent with detection?
rows: Yes: injection at the read position. Up to two injectors, 3–500 µL, up to 420 µL/s; <30 µL dead volume; clear, user-replaceable tubing.
With the injection spoon fitted and lens protect off, the reader injects during measurement; no post-injection delay for true flash luminescence.
Not published. The 77-page user manual has no injector or dispenser specification.
The 2008 EnVision’s sensitive detectors had no “real time” dispense-and-read mode, only a “shortened interval.”
Yes: injection at the read position, recording 50 readings per second through the injection. Two injectors, 3–500 µL, up to 420 µL/s, 0.5 mL prime. Any format to 1536.

No: luminescence reads wait “500 msec after injection ends” (800 ms for absorbance). Injectors not usable in FP or TRF; prime “at least 2 mL” plus 250 µL; plates must be unlidded; a PC is required for any injector protocol.
Peristaltic pumps: “The lifetime of the tubing is limited and you must replace the tubing when worn.” Accuracy ±(4% + 1 µL), so ≥14% at 10 µL (calculated).

Injectors to 384 from an external dispense module; the manual says only that the tips go into “holes inside the reader” and gives no tip-to-optics position or dispense-to-read delay (the Neo2 manual gives one). Dead volume 1.1 mL; “minimum recommended prime volume is 2000 μL.”
Opaque tubing and tips out of sight; a poor fit for shared equipment.

Injectors to 384 only, one well at a time, from an external module. Manual: the tips seat in holes inside the reader “behind the filter cube chamber(s)”; it specifies a maximum delay of < 1.0 second between end of dispense and start of read. Minimum prime 2,000 µL.

The manual never says the plate moves between dispense and read, or that the reader reads during injection; it gives only the tip location and the delay figure (p. 151, 96/384-well, default probe heights).
No. Injection position is away from the optics; the plate travels between inject and read. External module, opaque tubing, dead volume ≤100 µL.
The first light of a flash reaction happens where nothing is looking.
No. Injection happens away from the read position: the reagent is added, then the well is read. Back-flush, heater and stirrer.

Only with the dispensing head placed in the L position by hand. In the wrong position: “an extra plate movement… This may cause minor time delays between dispensing and measurement.” No dispensing with lidded-plate adapters or in 1536. Dead volume <100 µL.

tables.caption: Time-resolved fluorescence sensitivity (europium)
rows: <20 fM (384, 80 µL; <1.6 amol/well) with the Ultra HTRF/TRF module. Xenon flash lamp.
Laser <4 fM (0.004 pM); lamp <20 fM (15 µL ProxiPlate). Laser is an option: diode-pumped solid state, 343 nm, “< 200 µJ” per pulse.
Field experience: a diode source, and not that powerful. A pharma site’s 2023 demo never tested the laser: “our unit laser was broken.”
Laser TRF: <5 fM (384, 80 µL; 0.4 amol/well), on a dedicated red-shifted PMT pair. HTRF Delta F >1100%.
Best TRF figure published on any reader in this matrix (tied with the Neo2 laser’s 5 fM, which is a typical in a different plate).
iD5 only. Standard 150 fM guaranteed; with the Enhanced TRF module 100 fM guaranteed, 10 fM optimized. iD3: not offered.
The module is fitted by the customer with a 2.0 mm hex key, instrument powered on. TRF module must be removed if some non TRF-modes are read. Not appropriate for shared equipment
Data sheet <40 fM (no plate). Manual guarantee ≤250 fM, 96-well, more than 6× worse (calculated). Flash lamp; no laser offered.
5 fM with the TRF laser, 40 fM with the lamp (384 low-volume, typical). Manual lamp figure: “≤ 250 fM (100 fM typical).” Laser ships only on Dual Filter Top builds, 7 of 19 part numbers.
Single Filter Top readers never get the laser, and the manual still sells it as “upgrade later.”
Filters ≤4 amol (100 µL) = 40 fM standard; ≤0.5 amol (20 µL) = 25 fM enhanced. Monochromator ≤10 amol / ≤0.7 amol. Flash lamp only; no laser. Calculated.
<30 fM (384, 80 µL; <2.4 amol/well). Flash lamp, filters.
<1 amol per well (white low-volume 384; volume not stated) = 50 fM at 20 µL (calculated). Fixed 334 nm excitation filter; flash lamp.
